A total of 123 individuals were collected, belonging to five genera and nine species of dung beetles. Dung beetle assemblage had more species of small to medium body size (< 8 mm), with only two species classified as large-bodied. Large and small telecoprids were the most abundant functional groups. The mean (± SE) values for dung removal and soil excavation were 10.9 ± 2.33 g and 15.2 ± 4.22 g, respectively. These findings indicate that only a limited number of dung beetle species are able to colonize exotic pastures in the Southwestern Amazon, predominantly those of small to medium body size, which leads to a reduction of key ecological functions in these environments.

title: Recurrent High-Resolution Satellite Observations Quantify Facility-Resolved Annual Large-Emitter Methane Emissions in the Permian Basin
summary: Repeated high-resolution satellite observations can identify large methane emissions from individual oil and gas facilities, but sparse sampling, intermittent emissions, and variable observation conditions complicate the estimation of annua
content: Repeated high-resolution satellite observations can identify large methane emissions from individual oil and gas facilities, but sparse sampling, intermittent emissions, and variable observation conditions complicate the estimation of annual facility-level emissions. We develop an empirical hierarchical Bayesian method to estimate facility-resolved annual large-emitter methane emissions, with uncertainty, from repeated satellite plume detections and non-detections that were attributed to individual facilities. We apply the method to approximately 100,000 upstream and midstream facilities in the Permian Basin observed by the GHGSat satellite constellation from 2023 through 2025. Mean annual large-emitter emission rates differed strongly by facility class, averaging approximately 0.46 kg h⁻¹ for wells, 32–36 kg h⁻¹ for compressor/gathering stations, and 139–144 kg h⁻¹ for gas processing plants. Mean large-emitter persistence was approximately 0.001 for wells, 0.089–0.091 for compressor/gathering stations, and 0.238–0.249 for gas processing plants. Facility-level estimates were moderately heavy-tailed, with approximately 30–35% of midstream facilities accounting for 50% of estimated annual large-emitter emissions. Class-level mean estimates varied little between years, and more than 98% of matched midstream facilities showed no interannual change exceeding the combined estimation uncertainty. Summed and extrapolated facility estimates for the considered facility classes yielded GHGSat-derived Permian Basin totals of 1.70, 1.66, and 1.63 Mt y⁻¹ for 2023, 2024, and 2025, respectively. These results demonstrate that recurrent satellite observations can support facility-resolved, uncertainty-quantified estimates of the annual contribution from large methane emission events. The framework complements ground and aerial measurements, regional atmospheric inversions, and bottom-up inventories by providing repeated, attributable measurements across large facility populations.

title: Acquisition Time–Specific Deep Learning–Guided Image Quality Restoration in Accelerated I-123 DaTSCAN Brain SPECT on a Ring-Shaped CZT-Based Camera
source: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine
summary: Brain single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) imaging using I-123 DaTSCAN is an effective tool for the diagnosis and follow-up of Parkinson disease. Reducing acquisition time decreases the likelihood of patient motion, improves p
content: Brain single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) imaging using I-123 DaTSCAN is an effective tool for the diagnosis and follow-up of Parkinson disease. Reducing acquisition time decreases the likelihood of patient motion, improves patient comfort, and increases scanner throughput. However, shorter acquisition times often result in degraded image quality with reduced diagnostic value. This study aimed to use deep learning (DL) approaches to enhance the image quality of accelerated SPECT DaTSCAN acquisitions. A total of 85 patients were scanned on a CZT-based GE StarGuide scanner with a standard acquisition time of 15 min. To simulate fast acquisition protocols, raw list-mode data were retrospectively undersampled to represent 20%, 25%, and 50% of the original acquisition time and then reconstructed using the clinical routine protocol. A modified U-Net DL architecture incorporating attention and transformer mechanisms was trained to convert the low-count images into full-time equivalents. The output images were compared to full-time reference images using subjective image quality assessment by nuclear medicine physicians as well as region-wise and voxel-wise quantitative metrics on the test set. Both voxel-wise and region-wise metrics showed significant improvement when using the DL models for all fast acquisition times. Subjective image quality evaluations confirmed that the DL-predicted images were noticeably superior to the original low-count reconstructions in terms of perceived image quality and diagnostic confidence. The mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was reduced from ~ 30 to ~ 18% for fast 1/5 acquisition time images and from ~ 26 to ~ 16% for 1/4 acquisition time images. Our acquisition time-specific deep learning models effectively restore information loss in fast SPECT acquisitions and reduce image noise, without compromising diagnostic value. The models offer a promising approach for faster, patient-friendly brain SPECT imaging without sacrificing image quality or quantitative accuracy.

title: Synthesis of iodates from earth-abundant elements: Antiviral properties and textile applications
source: Journal of the Ceramic Society of Japan
summary: To develop inorganic antiviral materials that do not rely on rare-earth elements, iodate compounds composed of relatively earth-abundant elements were synthesized and evaluated. In addition, coating textile fibers using their released ionic
content: To develop inorganic antiviral materials that do not rely on rare-earth elements, iodate compounds composed of relatively earth-abundant elements were synthesized and evaluated. In addition, coating textile fibers using their released ionic species was investigated. Powder samples of Al(IO3)3, Cu(IO3)2, Mn(IO3)2, and Y(IO3)3 (prepared for comparison) were all confirmed to be single-phase and exhibited a certain solubility in water. Antiviral activity was evaluated against two types of viruses with distinct characteristics (non-enveloped and enveloped), following ISO-based protocols. All samples showed high antiviral activity against enveloped viruses, whereas Y(IO3)3 and Cu(IO3)2 also exhibited high activity against non-enveloped viruses. These results are attributed not only to the oxidative capability of IO3− ions but also to synergistic effects of coexisting cations, including charge neutralization at the viral surface, protein denaturation, and structural distortion. Furthermore, all materials were confirmed to exhibit low cytotoxicity. In coating experiments on cotton fibers, aqueous solutions containing the released ions together with a commercially available PVA-based textile sizing agent were used. Antiviral performance comparable to that of the corresponding powders was obtained for all samples except Al(IO3)3. Notably, cotton fibers treated with the coating solution derived from Al(IO3)3 exhibited high antiviral activity even against non-enveloped viruses, likely attributable to the solution pH. These findings indicate that iodate-based materials composed of earth-abundant elements—particularly Cu(IO3)2—are promising candidates for practical antiviral applications, and highlight the importance of ion-mediated mechanisms in coating systems.

title: Hydrotreating of Methyl Laurate and Crude Coconut Oil over PtSn/MgO/ZSM-5 Catalysts
source: Journal of the Japan Petroleum Institute
summary: The involvement of base sites in the deoxygenation pathways of fatty acid methyl esters, were investigated using a series of PtSn/MgO(m)/ZSM-5 (m = 1, 2.5, and 5 wt%) bifunctional catalysts were prepared by incipient wetness impregnation an
content: The involvement of base sites in the deoxygenation pathways of fatty acid methyl esters, were investigated using a series of PtSn/MgO(m)/ZSM-5 (m = 1, 2.5, and 5 wt%) bifunctional catalysts were prepared by incipient wetness impregnation and applied to the hydrotreating of methyl laurate (ML) and crude coconut oil (CCO). Higher MgO content decreased Brønsted acidity and suppressed the reducibility of Sn species, indicating strong metal-support and acid-base interactions. Catalytic evaluation in a continuous fixed-bed reactor revealed that PtSn/ZSM-5 favored the hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) pathway for ML, whereas MgO-modified catalysts progressively shifted the reaction toward decarboxylation (DCO) through selective modification of the acid-base site balance and hydrogen availability. Single-step hydrotreating of CCO over PtSn/MgO(2.5)/HZSM-5 achieved a C8-C16 hydrocarbon yield of 30.4 % at 375 °C, 1 MPa, a hydrogen/CCO ratio of 500 mL mL−1, and a WHSV of 1.5 h−1, and suppressed excessive cracking and light gas formation. The product consisted mainly of paraffins (80.9 wt%), with low oxygenates (<1 wt%) and moderate olefins (4.7 wt%). MgO addition reduced hydrogen consumption by optimizing the acidity and promoting the DCO pathway, indicating more effective design of hydrogen-efficient bifunctional catalysts for selective and sustainable aviation fuel production.

title: Temporal Misrecognition
source: The Journal of Public Interest Communications
summary: Environmental governance decisions are inherently communicative, shaping how risks, responsibilities and public interests are defined and justified. This paper examines how future generations are recognized within environmental governance,
content: Environmental governance decisions are inherently communicative, shaping how risks, responsibilities and public interests are defined and justified. This paper examines how future generations are recognized within environmental governance, using Western Australia as an empirical case. Drawing on recognition theory, climate ethics and public interest communications scholarship, it conceptualizes their exclusion as temporal misrecognition: acknowledgement without meaningful standing in decision-making. Analysis of Environmental Protection Authority reports and Office of the Appeals Convenor decisions from 2021 to 2025 finds that intergenerational equity and sustainability are routinely invoked but rarely carry substantive weight. The paper argues that public interest must be understood temporally and considers how future-oriented institutional mechanisms might make long-term impacts more visible, contestable and accountable.

title: Adaptive-CGAN: a comprehensive framework for generative modeling on google cloud platform
summary: Abstract Machine learning has become increasingly important in medical diagnosis, yet its effectiveness depends on access to large, reliable, and high-quality datasets. During epidemics and emerging diseases, such as COVID-19, acquiring suf
content: Abstract Machine learning has become increasingly important in medical diagnosis, yet its effectiveness depends on access to large, reliable, and high-quality datasets. During epidemics and emerging diseases, such as COVID-19, acquiring sufficient real-world medical images rapidly is challenging. To address these issues, this study presents an Adaptive Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (Adaptive-CGAN) integrated with a cloud-based medical image processing framework. The proposed approach makes three main contributions. First, Adaptive-CGAN generates high-fidelity synthetic medical images that closely resemble real samples while improving the distinction between real and fake images. Second, a scalable TensorFlow Records (TFRecords)-based pipeline is implemented on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) to support efficient storage, loading, and processing of large-scale medical datasets. Third, a real-world COVID-19 medical image dataset comprising four disease classes is compiled and used to enhance diagnostic prediction. Experimental evaluation was conducted against several baseline generative models, including AC-GAN, WGAN, Pix2Pix, BigGAN, and CWGAN, with AC-GAN serving as the primary like-for-like baseline. Adaptive-CGAN improved classification accuracy from 93.75% ± 1.10% to 99.60% ± 0.40%, increased the Inception Score from 7.20 ± 0.28 to 8.47 ± 0.18 (+ 17.65%), reduced FID from 28.41 ± 1.35 to 26.13 ± 0.82 (− 8.02%), and reduced KID from 0.0156 ± 0.0021 to 0.0143 ± 0.0015 (− 8.33%). Adaptive-CGAN also reduced training time by 15.8% and CO₂ emissions by 9.5% compared with AC-GAN. Moreover, the GCP-based Adaptive-CGAN deployment emitted only 0.0023 kg CO₂, compared with 0.0047 kg CO₂ for the local setup, representing an approximately 50% reduction due to optimized cloud execution and the TFRecord-based pipeline. These results demonstrate that Adaptive-CGAN can improve diagnostic performance, synthetic image quality, computational efficiency, and environmental sustainability in AI-assisted healthcare.

title: A silver nanoparticles based anti-fungal peptides system for fruit preservation: synthesis, characterization, applications and safety
summary: Food security is a growing global concern, with postharvest losses significantly affecting fruit and vegetables availability. A major factor contributing to these losses is microbial contamination, which necessitates the development of effe
content: Food security is a growing global concern, with postharvest losses significantly affecting fruit and vegetables availability. A major factor contributing to these losses is microbial contamination, which necessitates the development of effective and sustainable preservation techniques. Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) have appeared as promising antimicrobial agents due to their high stability and broad-spectrum activity. This review critically examines the synthesis, characterization, and antifungal efficacy of AgNPs, particularly in combination with natural antifungal peptides and phytochemicals. Various synthesis methods, including chemical, biological, and physical approaches, are explored, highlighting the advantages of green synthesis for eco-friendly applications. The molecular mechanisms of AgNPs-induced antimicrobial action, with emphasis on membrane disruption, reactive oxygen species generation, and intracellular damage. The synergistic effects in edible coating films, and their role in extending shelf life by inhibiting microbial growth are analyzed. Additionally, the combination of AgNPs with biodegradable polymers and their influence on food safety are discussed. While AgNPs offer significant potential in food preservation, challenges related to regulatory, toxicity, and safety approval must be addressed to ensure their widespread application. Future study should focus on optimizing nanoparticle synthesis for enhanced stability, reduced toxicity, and improved biocompatibility.

title: Full-Chain Commercialization Trends in CCUS and Their Implications for Korea: A Review of IEAGHG Technical Reports
source: Journal of the Korean Society of Mineral and Energy Resources Engineers
summary: In 2025, the global energy supply exceeded 600 EJ, and energy-sector CO 2 emissions reached 35.8 GtCO 2 , increasing the importance of carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) for addressing process and residual emissions in hard-to-
content: In 2025, the global energy supply exceeded 600 EJ, and energy-sector CO 2 emissions reached 35.8 GtCO 2 , increasing the importance of carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) for addressing process and residual emissions in hard-to-abate industries.This review examines full-chain commercialization trends in CCUS, focusing on the carbon capture and storage (CCS) value chain, where demonstration and deployment are most advanced.Analysis of technical reports published by the International Energy Agency Greenhouse Gas R&D Technology Collaboration Programme (IEAGHG) in 2025 and 2026, together with relevant field cases, identified key issues.These include industrial integration, air quality impacts, modularization, transport and storage costs and availability, flow metering, storage-site performance verification, long-term monitoring and liability transfer, market and financing structures, and social acceptance.These findings indicate that CCUS represents a portfolio of technologies suited to selective applications rather than a universal substitute.In Korea, commercialization requires an integrated framework encompassing appraisal drilling, injection demonstrations, domestic and international storage portfolios, transport and storage networks, monitoring, reporting, and verification, life-cycle assessment, long-term liability arrangements, market models, and public trust.

title: In situ Ni(II) to Ni(0) Reduction Enables Catalytic H2 Generation from Fe(II)-bearing Minerals
summary: Hydrogen is industrially produced at a scale of 70 million tons annually, with the majority of it derived from steam-methane reforming, an intensely emissions-heavy process. Vast reservoirs of mineralogical Fe(II) in the Earth’s subsurface
content: Hydrogen is industrially produced at a scale of 70 million tons annually, with the majority of it derived from steam-methane reforming, an intensely emissions-heavy process. Vast reservoirs of mineralogical Fe(II) in the Earth’s subsurface and anthropogenic Fe(II) from steel slags represent an opportunity to stimulate mineralogical hydrogen by the reaction of hypoxic water with Fe(II)-rich phases, potentially allowing for both emissions-free and economically scalable hydrogen production. For select minerals, H 2 production from the coupled oxidation of Fe(II)-bearing solids is dramatically enhanced upon addition of Ni(II) ions, and mechanistic models posit that H 2 forms at co-precipitated Ni(II) sites bound to the ferrous substrate. Herein, we test this model by examining the temporal progression of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) driven by Fe(OH) 2 oxidation in presence of exogenous Ni(II). We find that Ni(II) is not the active catalyst, but instead serves as a pre-catalyst that is reduced in situ to metallic Ni(0) particles that then catalyze H 2 generation. This Ni(II) to Ni(0) conversion mechanism is also operative for hydrogen evolution from the mineral siderite (FeCO 3 ), suggesting that it may be a general mechanistic motif across ferrous minerals, which accelerates H 2 generation where HER is rate-limiting. These studies offer mechanistic insight into the in situ speciation of a catalyst commonly used for stimulated mineralogical hydrogen production, laying the foundation for further catalytic studies in the pursuit of evaluating and maximizing the potential of stimulated mineralogical hydrogen production.

title: Megathrust Earthquakes Amplify Coastal Wave Hazards in Cascadia Under Rising Sea Levels
summary: Along the Cascadia Subduction Zone, destructive megathrust earthquakes represent a significant coastal hazard. These events generate abrupt, meter-scale coseismic subsidence, instantaneously increasing relative sea level, inundation extent,
content: Along the Cascadia Subduction Zone, destructive megathrust earthquakes represent a significant coastal hazard. These events generate abrupt, meter-scale coseismic subsidence, instantaneously increasing relative sea level, inundation extent, and the reach of ocean waves. In the coming decades, eustatic sea level rise will continue to shift baseline coastal conditions, with the potential to change earthquake-driven coastal hazards. Here, we model how sea level rise, wave climate, and the magnitude and timing of coseismic subsidence interact to influence nearshore wave dynamics at 32 rocky coast sites spanning diverse morphologies along the Cascadia margin. We find that coseismic subsidence amplifies shoreline wave power by shifting wave action landward and reducing energy dissipation, despite an overall reduction in wave breaking. This amplification is strongly controlled by shore platform slope, with negligible increases along steep rocky coasts and multiple orders-of-magnitude increases for low-gradient platforms. These changes highlight the potential for increases in wave-driven coastal erosion and shoreline retreat following future earthquakes. The timing and persistence of these earthquake-driven hazards depend strongly on the sea level rise trajectory. Under a high-emissions scenario, accelerated sea level rise shifts the window of maximum earthquake-driven amplification toward the beginning of the century, increasing the potential of post-event recovery. Our results demonstrate that interactions between sea level rise and episodic coseismic subsidence create transient, but potentially long-lived, shifts in coastal wave energy regimes that can shape future coastal hazards and landscape evolution. This coupling between climate and solid-Earth processes reveals a previously unrecognized control on coastal change along tectonically active margins.

title: Self‐Powered NbTe 2 /MoS 2 Photodetectors With High‐Sensitivity for Potential Intelligent Underwater Imaging Applications
summary: ABSTRACT Underwater optical imaging, vital for marine exploration, faces the challenge of optical signal degradation caused by water absorption and scattering, necessitating photodetectors with high sensitivity and low noise. In this work,
content: ABSTRACT Underwater optical imaging, vital for marine exploration, faces the challenge of optical signal degradation caused by water absorption and scattering, necessitating photodetectors with high sensitivity and low noise. In this work, we report a vertically stacked two‐dimensional NbTe 2 /MoS 2 van der Waals heterojunction designed for self‐powered underwater photodetection. Owing to the strong built‐in electric field at the heterointerface, the device effectively suppresses dark current and achieves a high rectification ratio of 7.3 × 10 4 . The photodetector exhibits a self‐powered, broadband photoresponse spanning the visible to near‐infrared region, with a peak responsivity of 2.1 mA/W and a specific detectivity of 6.7 × 10 10 Jones at 405 nm, outperforming most reported self‐powered heterojunction photodetectors. Under reverse bias, the detectivity is further enhanced to 1.15 × 10 12 Jones due to the strengthened internal electric field. Additionally, the device demonstrates a rapid temporal response, featuring a rise time of ≈47 µs and a decay time of ≈52 µs, respectively. Notably, the NbTe 2 /MoS 2 photodetector exhibits high imaging fidelity in aquatic environments, enabling high‐definition imaging through a deep‐learning‐based restoration algorithm. These results position the NbTe 2 /MoS 2 heterojunction as a promising candidate for energy‐efficient, high‐sensitivity underwater optoelectronics, advancing the field of intelligent underwater imaging.

title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Enterprise Resource Planning Systems: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Research Directions
summary: Enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems have come a long way since their inception in 1989 and have grown from transaction processing systems to intelligent enterprise systems with the help of artificial intelligence (AI). This study aim
content: Enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems have come a long way since their inception in 1989 and have grown from transaction processing systems to intelligent enterprise systems with the help of artificial intelligence (AI). This study aims to conduct a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of the current literature on the integration of AI in ERP systems from 1989 to 2026. Based on the PRISMA framework, relevant publications are identified in the major scientific databases in the context of bibliometric and thematic analyses, which highlight trends, impactful participants, new technologies, application fields, and future research directions. The review shows that research on AI-driven ERP is growing at a rapid pace, especially in recent years due to the development of machine learning, deep learning, NLP, generative AI, intelligent automation, and predictive analytics. The primary applications include finance, supply chain management, manufacturing, human resources, customer relationship management, and decision support. The study also presents a set of key research gaps on data governance, cybersecurity, interoperability, sustainable ERP, and human-AI collaboration, and outlines a conceptual framework and future research agenda to guide the creation of intelligent, trustworthy, and autonomous ERP ecosystems.

title: Wildfire Effects on the Geotechnical Properties of Soils: A State-of-the-Art Review
summary: Abstract Wildfires are becoming increasingly common in most parts of the world, posing significant risks to both the natural and built environment. Evidence also suggests that climate change is intensifying the frequency and severity of the
content: Abstract Wildfires are becoming increasingly common in most parts of the world, posing significant risks to both the natural and built environment. Evidence also suggests that climate change is intensifying the frequency and severity of these events. While the ecological and environmental impacts of wildfires have been thoroughly discussed, there is currently a lack of literature pertaining to their effects on the geotechnical properties and behaviors of soil, despite increasing evidence of their significance. This paper seeks to address this gap by presenting a state-of-the-art review of wildfire impacts and characterization methods, with particular emphasis on their implications in geotechnical engineering. Key concepts in wildfire characterization such as fire intensity and burn severity are discussed and the distinction between the two is highlighted. Various methods to assess burn severity are compared and the lack of standardization across approaches is raised. The review then discusses wildfire-induced changes in some key soil properties such as cohesion, internal friction angle, grain-size distribution, hydraulic conductivity, and hydrophobicity. Inconsistent trends in changes of these properties due to variability in pre-burn conditions, soil types, and fire characteristics are highlighted and the reasons for these inconsistencies are theorized. Furthermore, we identify key knowledge gaps in the existing literature and suggest potential avenues for future studies. We highlight the need to develop a burn severity criterion for geotechnical engineering applications as well as further investigations into wildfire-induced subsequent natural hazards such as landslides and erosion.

title: Electronic Fraud and Financial Performance of Banks: Experience from Nigeria
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF BANKING AND FINANCE RESEARCH
summary: This research work investigated the effect of electronic fraud on the financial performance of banks in Nigeria. The specific objectives were: to investigate the effect of wire fraud on the financial performance of banks in Nigeria, to eval
content: This research work investigated the effect of electronic fraud on the financial performance of banks in Nigeria. The specific objectives were: to investigate the effect of wire fraud on the financial performance of banks in Nigeria, to evaluate the effect of securities fraud on the financial performance of banks in Nigeria, and to determine the effect of credit card fraud on the financial performance of banks in Nigeria. The study adopted the ex post facto research method with panel data. The analytical technique adopted was the panel least squares regression method. The summary of the major findings of the study are: the study found that amounts lost to fraud through wire transfer has significant negative effect on financial performance of selected deposit money banks in Nigeria. [coefficient = -3.015834, with p-value of 0.0003]; the study found that amount lost to fraud through securities transaction has significant negative effect on financial performance of selected deposit money banks in Nigeria. [coefficient =-8.010412, with a p-value of 0.0417], and the study found that that amount lost to fraud through credit card transactions has negative insignificant effect on financial performance of selected deposit money banks in Nigeria. [coefficient = -1.380107 with a p-value of 0.3041]. The study concluded that electronic fraud has significant negative effect on the financial performance of banks especially with regards to the total assets. Based on the findings, the study recommended that: the banks should take steps to strictly monitor wire transactions to be able to detect fraudulent wire calls, the banks should place a hold on securities transactions that are traceable to Ponzi schemes; and the banks should make efforts to help customers protect their credit cards.

title: Do International Trade and Institutional Quality Improve Foreign Exchange Reserves? An Econometric Diagnosis
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
summary: This study investigates the effects of international trade and institutional quality on foreign exchange reserves in Nigeria. The study is focused on 1990 to 2022. Foreign exchange reserve of Nigeria is utilised as the dependent variable wh
content: This study investigates the effects of international trade and institutional quality on foreign exchange reserves in Nigeria. The study is focused on 1990 to 2022. Foreign exchange reserve of Nigeria is utilised as the dependent variable while international trade and institutional quality are indexed as net oil exports, net non-oil exports, real exchange rate, degree of trade openness and institutional quality index. Annual time-series data employed were sourced from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Statistical Bulletin, National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) Reports and World Development Indicators (WDI). Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) is the main technique of data analysis applied, and the study found that net oil exports and trade openness had favourable and substantial effects on foreign reserves accumulation in Nigeria, net non-oil exports appeared insubstantial but favourable on foreign reserves in Nigeria, real exchange rate had substantial adverse effect on foreign earnings reserves while institutional quality index had favourable and insubstantial effects on the regressand. The study concluded that international trade and institutional quality are in no small measure imperative contributors to accumulating foreign reserves in Nigeria. The study recommended that government should implement policies that incentivize the non-oil sector, such as providing tax breaks, subsidies, and infrastructure support to boost production for export. Hence, strategic partnerships with global markets can further enhance Nigeria’s competitiveness in the non-oil sector, which in the long term would expectedly improve Nigeria’s external reserves.

title: Nanomaterials in biolubricant synthesis from vegetable oils: A systematic review of nanoadditives and nanocatalysts
summary: Biomass-derived biolubricants offer an environmentally sustainable solution to shift from conventional mineral-based lubricants, addressing growing concerns over increasing carbon footprint, resource depletion, climate and environmental imp
content: Biomass-derived biolubricants offer an environmentally sustainable solution to shift from conventional mineral-based lubricants, addressing growing concerns over increasing carbon footprint, resource depletion, climate and environmental impact. This review systematically evaluates how application of various nanomaterials as both additives and heterogeneous catalysts improve the physiochemical properties, catalytic efficiency, tribological and rheological properties of biolubricants synthesized from edible and non-edible vegetable oils. A systematic literature search was conducted using Web of Science, Scopus and Google Scholar for studies published during 2015–2026 following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework. The identified records were screened and selected according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, and a total of 104 studies were included in the final review. The analysis established that nano additives provide excellent lubricity to vegetable oils by reducing friction and wear, while nanocatalysts enable fruitful yield of biodegradable polyol esters. By combining nanotechnology and renewable feedstocks, this review contributes theoretical insights into the recent developments in production of sustainable and high performed biolubricants. Future research should focus on development of sustainable bio-derived nanoadditives, improved nanoadditive dispersion and surface functionalization, comprehensive life-cycle and environmental toxicity assessment, and scalable catalyst/nanoadditive recovery and reuse.

title: The Electromagnetic Cascade: Wave Structure, Spectral Architecture, and the Hydrogen Spectrum from Bilateral Stella Geometry
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The Electromagnetic Cascade: Wave Structure, Spectral Architecture, and the Hydrogen Spectrum from Bilateral Stella Geometry Kevin Birke Packler1 & Claude Sonnet 4.62 (Anthropic) 1Aureole Foundation, Wake Forest, NC 2Anthropic AI Systems Co
content: The Electromagnetic Cascade: Wave Structure, Spectral Architecture, and the Hydrogen Spectrum from Bilateral Stella Geometry Kevin Birke Packler1 & Claude Sonnet 4.62 (Anthropic) 1Aureole Foundation, Wake Forest, NC 2Anthropic AI Systems Companion to Cosmic Egg Theory v22·September 2026 Abstract We derive the full wave structure of the electromagnetic field from the bilateral Stella geometry established in Cosmic Egg Theory v22, closing four formal gaps left open by that framework and recovering the spectral architecture of classical and quantum electrodynamics without additional postulates. Beginning from the bilateral substrate field equation □Φ = 0 and the parity constraint Φ(−x,t) = Φ(x,t), we prove that the only bilateral-symmetric solu- tions are standing waves—identifying particles as symmetric-sector resonances of the bilateral field. Propagating electromagnetic waves are shown to be bilateral- symmetry-breaking excitations left in the substrate by a moving Stella, with dis- persion relation ω= ck forced by the ground-state geometry. Extending the scalar treatment to the bilateral 4-vector field Aµ, we show that the Lorenz gauge condition ∂µAµ = 0 is a direct consequence of the bilateral balance condition established in Step 8 of CET. The photon polarization count Npol = 2 is proved via a Span Theorem on the Stella’s four tetrahedral axis pro- jections. Circular polarization states are identified with the T1 and T2 tetrahedra; photon spin ±ℏ follows from the 60◦bilateral rotation of Step 4. The cascade-frequency correspondence λN = 2πℓP·2N establishes that each step in the Packler attenuation cascade corresponds to one octave in electromag- netic frequency. Wien’s displacement law, the Stefan-Boltzmann T4 radiation law, and the Planck distribution are recovered as direct consequences of the cascademode structure and bilateral occupation statistics. The Rydberg formula is expressed in cascade coordinates as Nγ(n1,n2) = RCET−log2(1/n2 1−1/n2 2), where RCET = Ne+ 1 + 2 log2(α−1). Fifteen hydrogen emission lines spanning five spectral series are confirmed to sub-percent precision. The virial theorem ⟨T⟩= 1 2 |⟨V⟩|for Coulomb binding is derived directly from the bilateral balance condition, closing the ”+1” in RCET from pure bilateral geometry with no classical mechanics import. Four Zero Free Parameter results are established or upgraded: Wien’s dis- placement law (zfp Row 22), the Stefan-Boltzmann T4 law (zfp Row 23), the Rydberg cascade formula (zfp Row 24), the virial theorem for bilateral bound states (zfp Row 25), and the polarization count upgraded from stated to proved (zfp Row 20 upgrade). No free parameters are introduced beyond those already entering v22.

title: Electrified integrated gas-to-liquids enables decentralized sustainable aviation fuel production from biogas and CO2
summary: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production from distributed biogenic carbon resources remains limited by the high capital intensity and process complexity of conventional gas-to-liquids (GTL) technologies. Here, we report the development an
content: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production from distributed biogenic carbon resources remains limited by the high capital intensity and process complexity of conventional gas-to-liquids (GTL) technologies. Here, we report the development and pilot-scale validation of Cool GTL™, an electrified, integrated GTL platform designed for the decentralized conversion of biogenic gas and CO2-derived carbon into drop-in transportation fuels. The process combines an internally electrically heated reformer, Fischer–Tropsch (FT) synthesis, and direct product upgrading in a compact configuration that eliminates external fired reformers, intermediate syngas conditioning, and stand-alone hydrocracking. The electrically heated reformer simultaneously converts CH4, C2⁺ hydrocarbons, steam, and CO2 through bi-reforming to produce synthesis gas with an H2/CO ratio of 2.0–2.55, enabling direct FT conversion without downstream adjustment. Unlike conventional GTL systems, the integrated upgrading reactor enables hydrocracking and hydroisomerization directly in the presence of CO, eliminating the need for CO removal and reducing the requirement for high-purity hydrogen supply. The fully integrated pilot plant demonstrated stable operation for more than 2,400 h using multiple carbon feedstocks and produced over 190 L of liquid hydrocarbons, with approximately 50 wt% distributed in the SAF boiling range. The optimized SAF fraction satisfied applicable ASTM fuel specifications, including freeze-point requirements. Compared with scaled-down conventional GTL designs, the simplified configuration reduced estimated capital cost by approximately 78% for a 2,500 bbl/d system. These results demonstrate an electrified, low-complexity GTL pathway that enables economically attractive decentralized production of SAF from biogenic carbon and CO2.

title: Drugs Destroyed in Intensive Care and Their Annual Financial Burden
summary: Purpose: Unused medications can be considered a waste of resources. By reducing waste, the cost of healthcare services can be lowered without compromising the quality of patient care. This study aims to measure pharmaceutical waste in inten
content: Purpose: Unused medications can be considered a waste of resources. By reducing waste, the cost of healthcare services can be lowered without compromising the quality of patient care. This study aims to measure pharmaceutical waste in intensive care, draw attention to the economic dimension of waste, identify the causes of waste, and discuss possible preventive measures.Materials and Methods: In a tertiary care unit with 15 beds at Adana City Hospital, the wasted drugs in one year were prospectively recorded.Results: In a tertiary care unit where 1245 patients were treated in one year, the total cost of drugs annually was 226241.7 TL (approximately 5258 US dollars). Enteral nutrition solutions were the most wasted drug by volume, accounting for 33% of wasted drug volume. Levofloxacin caused the greatest cost loss among the wasted drugs, accounting for 18.4% of the total wasted drug cost. At least one drug was wasted in 30.4% (n=379/1245) of the patients. A total of 580 drug waste events were recorded. Disposal was detected in drugs with 26 different active ingredients. The most common reasons for drug waste were identified as: disposal of diluted solutions (59.7%, n=346), disposal of partially used drugs due to lack of small doses (31.7%, n=184), and disposal of contaminated drugs (8.6%, n=50).Conclusion: Identifying the causes of waste is essential for initiating preventive measures. The extent and causes of drug waste should be determined in each clinic, and waste reduction strategies should be developed by optimizing drug preparation.

title: Low-carbon energy production for sustainable development: a bibliometric analysis and SWOT appraisal of artificial intelligence contributions
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is positioned as a strategic enabler of low-carbon and renewable energy systems, yet the knowledge base at this intersection has expanded more rapidly than it has consolidated. This study examines the evolving l
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) is positioned as a strategic enabler of low-carbon and renewable energy systems, yet the knowledge base at this intersection has expanded more rapidly than it has consolidated. This study examines the evolving landscape through a Scopus-based bibliometric analysis combined with a SWOT appraisal to clarify how AI is contributing to low-carbon and renewable energy production for sustainable development. The review integrates descriptive performance analysis and science mapping, including bibliographic coupling, citation, co-authorship, co-citation, and keyword co-occurrence. Available evidence were extended through a coded core sample used for strategic interpretation. The findings show that the field has moved from an emerging niche into a rapidly expanding research domain, with annual scientific output rising from 239 documents in 2021 to 2,366 in 2025. Its technical core is strongly concentrated around machine learning and deep learning, particularly in forecasting/prediction and optimization. The corpus contains 5,192 documents linked to sustainable development.

title: When beliefs meet technology: conservatism, climate denialism, and support for solar geoengineering
summary: Solar geoengineering is an object of deep political contestation. Public responses to solar geoengineering technologies cannot be as easily explained by political ideology alone. Hypothesizing that climate denialism mediates ideology’s infl
content: Solar geoengineering is an object of deep political contestation. Public responses to solar geoengineering technologies cannot be as easily explained by political ideology alone. Hypothesizing that climate denialism mediates ideology’s influence on public support for solar geoengineering, we ask: (1) What is the relationship between political conservatism and support for solar geoengineering, and does it differ by country and technology? (2) Is this relationship mediated by climate denialism? We answer these questions using mediation analyses of public attitudes toward three climate intervention technologies across thirteen countries. Our findings show that conservatives are generally less supportive of solar geoengineering, and this opposition is largely rooted in climate denialism with variation across technologies. Once denialism is controlled for, conservatism is associated with greater support for certain technologies in some countries but not others. Therefore, the relationship between conservatism and climate intervention support does not reflect a single, stable ideological association.

title: Aligning academic artificial intelligence research with the national innovation strategy of Saudi Arabia under vision 2030
summary: This study explores how academic research on artificial intelligence (AI) in Saudi Arabia aligns with the country’s strategic goals for innovation and digital transformation under Vision 2030. Despite substantial investments in AI, there re
content: This study explores how academic research on artificial intelligence (AI) in Saudi Arabia aligns with the country’s strategic goals for innovation and digital transformation under Vision 2030. Despite substantial investments in AI, there remains limited clarity on whether scholarly output effectively supports the innovation capacity and digital preparedness of key business sectors. The study adopts ten methodological steps from the bibliometric–systematic literature review (B-SLR) methodology, as outlined in previous literature. A total of 75 peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science database. VOSviewer was utilized to analyze keyword co-occurrence, temporal evolution, and bibliographic coupling. A thematic synthesis was derived from the systematic literature review (SLR). The analysis identified eight thematic clusters: core AI readiness; AI’s role in crisis management; data-driven significance; innovation and sustainability; national strategy and policy orientation; higher education; AI’s role in public health and decision-making; and AI in the finance sector. The SLR also pinpointed five cross-cutting themes: responsible AI, corporate digital responsibility (CDR), alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), regulatory governance, and workforce upskilling. Finally, bibliometric coupling positioned Saudi Arabia as an emerging contributor to global digitization, although collaboration within the Gulf region remains limited. This study adds to the literature on management information systems and strategic management by providing actionable insights for business leaders, policymakers, and academic institutions aiming to foster research-strategy alignment and enhance sectoral capacity for AI adoption in emerging economies.

title: WHOLE LIFE CARBON-BASED ANALYSIS OF THE 2050 NET-ZERO SCENARIO IN AN EXISTING URBAN DISTRICT
source: Journal of Environmental Engineering (Transactions of AIJ)
summary: Whole life carbon (WLC) assessment toward achieving net-zero by 2050 in existing urban districts were conducted. Four consecutive investigations were conducted: (1) an overview of decarbonization trends and methodological framework, (2) dat
content: Whole life carbon (WLC) assessment toward achieving net-zero by 2050 in existing urban districts were conducted. Four consecutive investigations were conducted: (1) an overview of decarbonization trends and methodological framework, (2) data collection of the target district and its building stock, (3) comparative WLC assessment of two scenarios—rebuilding after 60 years and retrofit-only—and (4) development of a Net-Zero District Priority Index (nZPI) integrating operational carbon, embodied carbon, and residual building lifetime. The findings emphasize the importance of retrofit-first approaches, life-cycle-based urban planning, and data-driven tools for managing WLC at the urban scale.

title: YENİLENEBİLİR ENERJİ, EKONOMİK BÜYÜME, KÜRESELLEŞME VE SABİT SERMAYENİN ÇEVRESEL BOZULMASI ÜZERİNDEKİ ETKİSİ: G7 EKONOMİLERİNDEN AMPİRİK KANITLAR
summary: G7 ekonomileri başta Paris Anlaşması olmak üzere birçok uluslararası iklim zirvesine katılmakla birlikte hala dünyanın en önemli CO2 salınımına sahip ekonomileri arasında yer almaktadırlar. Bu nedenle bu çalışma G7 ekonomilerinde yenilenebi
content: G7 ekonomileri başta Paris Anlaşması olmak üzere birçok uluslararası iklim zirvesine katılmakla birlikte hala dünyanın en önemli CO2 salınımına sahip ekonomileri arasında yer almaktadırlar. Bu nedenle bu çalışma G7 ekonomilerinde yenilenebilir enerji, küreselleşme, ekonomik büyüme ve sabit sermayenin CO2 emisyonları üzerindeki etkisini panel veri teknikleriyle 1990-2022 döneminde analiz etme amacını taşır. Bu çalışmada CADF birim kök testi ile Pedroni ve Westerlund eşbütünleşme testleri, panel AMG tahmincisi ve Dumitrescu–Hurlin nedensellik yaklaşımı kullanılmıştır. Elde edilen ampirik bulgular tüm değişkenler arasında bir dönemli bir ilişkinin varlığına işaret etmektedir. Uzun dönemde yenilenebilir enerji kullanımı CO2 emisyonlarını azaltarak çevresel bozulmayı azaltmaktadır. Ekonomik büyüme ve küreselleşme ise CO2 salınımlarını tetikleyerek çevresel bozulmayı artırmaktadır. Bulgular yenilenebilir enerji ile CO2 emisyonları arasında çift yönlü bir nedenselliğe işaret ederken ekonomik büyüme ve küreselleşmeden CO2 emisyonlarına doğru tek yönlü bir nedensellik kendisini göstermektedir. Bulgulara dayanarak G7 ekonomilerinde çevresel bozulmayı engelleyecek politika önerileri geliştirmek mümkündür. Ayrıca elde edilen sonuçlar, yenilenebilir enerji yatırımlarının artırılması ve çevre dostu teknolojilerin teşvik edilmesinin sürdürülebilir kalkınma hedefleri açısından kritik bir önem taşıdığını ortaya koymaktadır. Bu bağlamda, enerji politikalarının çevresel hassasiyetleri dikkate alacak şekilde yeniden yapılandırılması, uzun vadede hem ekonomik büyüme hem de çevresel koruma açısından fayda sağlayacaktır.

title: Impact of RbF Postdeposition Treatment Dose on Defects and the Barrier at the Back Contact in (Ag, Cu)(In, Ga)Se 2 Solar Cells
summary: The impact of RbF postdeposition treatment, including the influence of the total RbF dose, on bulk defects and the back contact barrier in (Ag, Cu)(In, Ga)Se 2 (ACIGS) solar cells is investigated. Deep level transient spectroscopy (DLTS) re
content: The impact of RbF postdeposition treatment, including the influence of the total RbF dose, on bulk defects and the back contact barrier in (Ag, Cu)(In, Ga)Se 2 (ACIGS) solar cells is investigated. Deep level transient spectroscopy (DLTS) reveals three signatures: H1, H2, and N1. H1 and H2 are attributed to hole traps within the material bulk, and N1 is attributed to the back contact barrier. The H2 trap acts as a recombination center and is found to affect the room temperature capacitance–voltage ( C – V ) results, necessitating “fast C – V ” measurements. The N1 signature has increasing activation energy (barrier height) with increasing RbF dose, and good quantitative agreement is obtained between energies measured using DLTS and admittance spectroscopy, as well as qualitative agreement with current–voltage–temperature ( J – V – T ) measurements. Macroscale SIMS and nanoscale transmission electron microscopy‐based X‐ray energy dispersive spectroscopy measurements reveal Rb accumulation at the ACIGS/MoSe 2 interface that increases, along with Rb concentration in the ACIGS bulk, with increasing RbF dose. The accumulation of compensating charges near this interface is proposed to be the explanation for the increased back contact barrier height observed here.

title: From pixels to ponds: assessing the feasibility of identifying small water features using satellite imagery
summary: Abstract Accurate information on the current extent and ecological condition of ponds is essential for effective conservation planning and implementation. However, such efforts are often limited by insufficient or outdated mapping. The use
content: Abstract Accurate information on the current extent and ecological condition of ponds is essential for effective conservation planning and implementation. However, such efforts are often limited by insufficient or outdated mapping. The use of remote sensing using satellites offers a potential mapping tool for these small features. This paper uses a case study from south-west England to assess the feasibility of using remote sensing to identify ponds examining the full remote sensing workflow including image availability, satellite sensor selection, costs and detection performance across multiple sensors and methods. Detection improved with increasing spatial resolution, with higher spatial resolution imagery enabling smaller ponds to be identified under optimal conditions but this incurred higher costs. However, across all methods, performance was limited by high rates of false positives and omission errors. Precision was consistently low, indicating that many detected ponds were not true ponds, while the proportion of real ponds correctly detected varied depending on the sensor and method used. Pond size, relative to satellite sensor pixel size, was the most influential factor in detectability and misclassification, with the presence of macrophytes also playing a key role. This research provides the first comprehensive assessment of the remote sensing workflow for pond detection in the UK and offers broader insights into identifying small landscape features. The findings support conservation and research efforts and serve as a practical guide for others seeking to apply these techniques in similar contexts.

title: When Digital Meets Green: Exploring Innovation and Integration Effects on Sustainable Performance in Food Supply Chains
summary: ABSTRACT According to information processing theory (IPT), the main objective of this study is to examine how digital technologies (DT) influence sustainable performance (SP). This study also examines the mediating role of green innovation
content: ABSTRACT According to information processing theory (IPT), the main objective of this study is to examine how digital technologies (DT) influence sustainable performance (SP). This study also examines the mediating role of green innovation (GI) between DT and SP and the moderating role of green integration between DT‐GI and DT‐SP. Data from 286 Chinese food supply chain SMEs (CFSC) are examined, and the hypothesis is tested using the Smart‐PLS software. The findings show that DT had a positive and significant impact on SP, and the mediating role of GI was also positive and significant between DT and SP. The results indicate that the relationship between DT and SP is significantly moderated by green integration compared with the relationship between DT and GI. The study's findings are associated with significant practical and theoretical implications for firms and management.

title: A dyed‐absorbance‐based framework for predicting and optimising reactive dye recipes in cotton fabric dyeing
summary: Abstract This study proposes a data‐driven framework for predicting and optimising reactive dye recipes in cotton fabric dyeing. The proposed approach introduces dyed‐absorbance as an empirical, reflectance‐derived spectral index for wavele
content: Abstract This study proposes a data‐driven framework for predicting and optimising reactive dye recipes in cotton fabric dyeing. The proposed approach introduces dyed‐absorbance as an empirical, reflectance‐derived spectral index for wavelength‐resolved spectral representation, rather than as a direct physical absorbance. The system predicts dye combinations from dyed‐absorbance spectra and subsequently estimates the corresponding concentrations. By integrating a Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short‐Term Memory (CNN‐LSTM) model with regression‐based mathematical correction grounded in wavelength‐dependent dyed‐absorbance behaviour, the system is intended to improve colour‐matching accuracy and reduce the number of redundant dyeing trials. Unlike conventional computer colour‐matching evaluation methods that rely on reflectance‐derived K/S values and extensive empirical calibration dyeing libraries, the proposed approach is designed to reduce reliance on accumulated calibration datasets by formulating wavelength‐dependent relationships between spectral features and dye concentration. The framework was evaluated in a representative production‐derived colour‐matching case using laboratory‐scale dyeing. The CMC colour difference (Δ E ) value decreased from 1.94 to 0.43, and metamerism indices under illuminants A and U3500 were reduced to 0.29 and 0.14, respectively. The proposed framework operates on standard computing platforms and is presented as a workflow for dye recipe prediction and correction.

title: Identifying eco-optimal nitrogen and irrigation management for wheat production in the North China Plain
summary: Intensive winter wheat production in the North China Plain (NCP) is increasingly constrained by excessive nitrogen (N) inputs, groundwater depletion, and environmental burdens. Identifying an optimal water-N management strategy that balance
content: Intensive winter wheat production in the North China Plain (NCP) is increasingly constrained by excessive nitrogen (N) inputs, groundwater depletion, and environmental burdens. Identifying an optimal water-N management strategy that balances productivity, profitability, energy performance, and environmental sustainability is therefore essential. A four-season split-plot field experiment was conducted under high–low seedbed cultivation (HLSC), with four N application rates (N1: 360, N2: 300, N3: 240, and N4: 180 kg N ha −1 ) assigned to the main plots and three irrigation quotas (W1: 120, W2: 90, and W3: 60 mm) assigned to the subplots. Economic performance, energy budgets, environmental impacts, and eco-efficiency were jointly assessed to identify an eco-optimal management strategy (EOMS). Across the four growing seasons, N3W2 provided the best overall balance among crop productivity, profitability, energy efficiency, and environmental sustainability. Grain yield under N3W2 was statistically comparable to that under the higher-input treatments, while achieving the highest net income (1370.89 $ ha −1 ) and benefit–cost ratio (1.61). Reducing N application from N1 to N3 decreased energy input by an average of 18.91% across irrigation levels, while N3W2 maintained a high energy-use efficiency (9.53). Compared with N1W1, N3W2 reduced the total normalized midpoint burden and total endpoint environmental damage by 25.9% and 24.1%, respectively. Fertilizer and irrigation were the dominant contributors to environmental burdens, jointly accounting for 91.3% of the summed normalized midpoint burden. N3W2 also achieved the highest endpoint eco-efficiency (2.20 $ Pt −1 ), demonstrating that coordinated reductions in water and N inputs can improve economic and environmental performance without a significant yield penalty. Overall, coupling 240 kg N ha −1 with 90 mm irrigation quotas provides a practical EOMS for HLSC-cultivated wheat in the NCP and other regions with comparable conditions.

title: Characterizing snow grain size and shape evolution across 20 scenarios of dry snow metamorphism
summary: Abstract. Snow microstructure evolves continuously during dry snow metamorphism, governing many effective physical properties of snow. Accurately representing this evolution in snowpack models requires objective descriptors of grain size an
content: Abstract. Snow microstructure evolves continuously during dry snow metamorphism, governing many effective physical properties of snow. Accurately representing this evolution in snowpack models requires objective descriptors of grain size and grain shape together with reliable temporal evolution laws. However, the evolution of snow microstructure has not been systematically characterized over the full range of dry snow metamorphism conditions. Here, we investigate the temporal evolution of several grain-size and grain-shape descriptors during dry snow metamorphism using a unique 4D X-ray tomography dataset comprising 20 experiments covering a broad range of temperatures, temperature gradients, and initial snow types. We analyze specific surface area (SSA), optical and microwave grain sizes, correlation length, structural anisotropy, three curvature-based grain-shape descriptors, as well as the full chord length and mean curvature distributions. Our results reveal that SSA evolution is far more diverse than generally assumed, including transient increases under strong temperature gradients. Optical and microwave grain-size descriptors often differ in both absolute value and temporal evolution, suggesting that snowpack models should predict both rather than a single grain-size descriptor. Vertical structural anisotropy does not systematically develop under temperature gradients, contrary to the common assumption. Overall, the initial snow microstructure strongly controls grain-shape evolution and, to a lesser extent, grain-size evolution, while both are also influenced by temperature gradient and mean temperature. These results provide new experimental constraints for developing and evaluating snow microstructure representations and temporal evolution laws in snowpack models. Future snowpack models could benefit from predicting the full chord length and mean curvature distributions rather than only scalar descriptors.

title: A Wearable Wireless Sensor Framework for Trial-by-Trial Validation of Audiovisual Stimulus Onset Asynchrony in Dynamic Virtual Reality
summary: Accurate control of stimuli timing is essential in psychophysical experiments, yet the stimulus onset asynchrony (SOA) specified within a virtual reality (VR) application may differ from that physically delivered to the participant. This st
content: Accurate control of stimuli timing is essential in psychophysical experiments, yet the stimulus onset asynchrony (SOA) specified within a virtual reality (VR) application may differ from that physically delivered to the participant. This study presents a wearable wireless sensor framework for measuring physical audiovisual SOAs on a trial-by-trial basis during VR experiments. Visual onset is detected using a photodiode-based synchronization marker, whereas auditory onset is detected directly from the analog audio signal using a portable wireless sensing module. The framework is characterized across different rendering pipelines, audio buffer configurations, spatial audio conditions, and wired and wireless headset connections, and subsequently validated during psychophysical experiments under both stationary and walking conditions. Before compensation, systematic audiovisual offsets ranged from 118 to 185 ms across configurations. Condition-specific temporal compensation reduced mean SOA errors to approximately zero, although residual trial-to-trial variability remained, with standard deviations of 11–32 ms. During psychophysical validation, the framework successfully measured physical audiovisual onset in 99.94\% of trials. These results demonstrate that trial-by-trial physical monitoring can complement conventional pre-experimental calibration, enabling behavioral responses to be associated with the audiovisual timing actually delivered on each trial and supporting more accurate and reproducible audiovisual psychophysics in dynamic VR.

title: Single Crystal Vibronic Spectroscopy of [Yb(trensal)]
summary: Understanding vibronic coupling in molecular materials is crucial in the development of high performance molecule-based optical and quantum technologies. Vibronic coupling governs spin state lifetimes in these systems, and is additionally a
content: Understanding vibronic coupling in molecular materials is crucial in the development of high performance molecule-based optical and quantum technologies. Vibronic coupling governs spin state lifetimes in these systems, and is additionally a source of decoherence. Hence, gaining detailed understanding of vibronic coupling will enable improvement of candidate materials. In this regard, magneto-spectroscopic techniques provide a direct probe of the vibronic coupling, which can be performed on polycrystalline and more recently single crystal samples. Single crystal magneto-spectroscopy offers a clear advantage due to its improved resolution and its ability to probe magnetic anisotropy, however, simulating the resulting spectra has proven difficult due to the simultaneous requirements of solid-state phonon calculations, embedded correlated electronic structure theory methods, and inclusion of large numbers of vibrational modes in the Hamiltonian to recreate experimental spectra. In this work we present single crystal far-infrared magneto-spectroscopy (FIRMS) and photo-luminescence magneto-spectroscopy (PLUMS) measurements on [Yb(trensal)] . We can experimentally verify previous assertions that most of the vibronic transitions in the FIRMS map are intra-Kramers doublet transitions and additionally elucidate the origin of the transitions observed in the PLUMS map. Crucially, to achieve this we have developed a new computational framework to perform robust and efficient simulations of magneto-spectroscopy incorporating hundreds of vibrational modes based on ab initio simulations in the solid state.

title: Havayolu sektöründe karbon açıklamalarının tematik yapısı: Küresel ölçekte bir içerik analizi
summary: Ulaştırma sektörü küresel karbon emisyonunun önemli bir kısmını oluşturmaktadır. Özellikle havacılık alanında sektörün yıllık büyüme oranı, fosil yakıt bağımlılığı gibi faktörler nedeniyle karbon emisyon değerleri artmaya devam etmektedir.
content: Ulaştırma sektörü küresel karbon emisyonunun önemli bir kısmını oluşturmaktadır. Özellikle havacılık alanında sektörün yıllık büyüme oranı, fosil yakıt bağımlılığı gibi faktörler nedeniyle karbon emisyon değerleri artmaya devam etmektedir. Bu nedenle havayolu firmalarının karbon ayak izlerine ait açıklama yapmaları ve paydaşlarına bilgi vermeleri beklenmektedir. Bu çalışmada uluslararası ölçekte piyasa değeri en yüksek 50 havayolu firmasının 2020–2024 dönemlerine ait finansal ve finansal olmayan raporlarında yer alan karbon açıklamaları içerik analizi yöntemiyle incelemesi amaçlanmıştır. Araştırmada 8 ana tema altında toplam 100 anahtar kelimeden oluşan bir analiz sözlüğü kullanılmıştır. Analizde 250 firma-yıl gözlemi için 86.000 sayfadan fazla rapor Python programı aracılığıyla analiz edilmiştir. Araştırma bulgularına göre farklı ülkelerdeki havayolu firmalarının raporlarında karbonla ilişkili anahtar kelimelerin kullanım sıklığı homojen değildir. İçerik analiz sonuçlarına göre anahtar kelime sıklıkları çoğunlukla temel karbon kavramları, sera gazı emisyonları ve havacılığa özgü karbonsuzlaştırma uygulamaları temalarında yoğunlaşmaktadır. Buna karşılık karbon açıklama ve raporlama, düzenleyici çerçeveler ve karbon piyasaları temalarındaki anahtar kelimeler raporlarda daha düşük sıklıkta yer almıştır. Ayrıca 2020–2024 döneminde karbonla ilişkili anahtar kelimelerin toplam sıklığında belirgin bir artış eğilimi görülmüştür. Ülke düzeyindeki analizlerde net sıfır hedefi koyan ülkelerde faaliyet gösteren havayolu firmalarının karbon açıklama puanı ve yoğunluk endeksi değerlerinin daha yüksek olduğu belirlenmiştir. Çalışma havayolu sektöründe karbon açıklamalarının tematik görünümünü ortaya koyarak literatüre katkı sunmaktadır.

title: Progress in PV, PV/T, and CPV Technologies: Thermal Management Strategies, Performances, Challenges, and Prospects
summary: The escalating demand for photovoltaic (PV) technologies across agriculture, industry, and even space exploration necessitates innovative solutions to combat performance degradation due to heat. This review delves into the latest advancemen
tags: Thermal management of electronic devices and systems
content: The escalating demand for photovoltaic (PV) technologies across agriculture, industry, and even space exploration necessitates innovative solutions to combat performance degradation due to heat. This review delves into the latest advancements in conventional PV, photovoltaic‐thermal (PV/T), and concentrated photovoltaic (CPV) systems, assessing the feasibility of thermal energy management strategies to enhance efficiency. The analysis of system configurations and cooling techniques yields significant insights into the optimization of performance. By 2025, silicon back‐contact cells have achieved 26% efficiency, hybrid interdigitated back‐contact cells reached 27.81%, TOPCon (tunnel‐oxide passivating contact) cells attained 27.79%, and silicon‐perovskite tandem cells hit 33%. PV/T systems showcased overall (electrical and thermal) energy conversion efficiencies of 70%–85%. CPV systems, leveraging advanced multijunction cells, achieve efficiencies of up to 47.6%, though effective thermal management is crucial at high concentration ratios. CPV/T systems are well‐suited for industrial combined heat and power applications, delivering 20%–28% electrical efficiency while capturing 60%–70% useful thermal energy. This comprehensive review also highlights effective design, material compatibility, feasibility, and reliability of various PV technologies. Scientific data generated from continued innovation in thermal management strategies will help meet the rising global demand for clean energy and support researchers, engineers, and policymakers in advancing the future of solar power.

title: XDOAS: A Unified Covariance–PCA DOAS Framework for Enhanced Trace Gas Retrievals – Application to OClO from TROPOMI
summary: Abstract. The treatment of the fit residual is a central problem in DOAS retrievals from hyperspectral satellite instruments. At the precision of instruments such as TROPOMI, the residual of a classical fit is no longer an approximately whi
content: Abstract. The treatment of the fit residual is a central problem in DOAS retrievals from hyperspectral satellite instruments. At the precision of instruments such as TROPOMI, the residual of a classical fit is no longer an approximately white background, but splits into systematic structures of physical and instrumental origin and a correlated random noise. Classical DOAS treats both in the same way, which limits its performance for weak absorbers retrieved under difficult conditions. This study presents XDOAS, a complete retrieval that unifies two recent approaches to this problem, covariance weighting and principal component analysis (PCA), within a single linear formulation. The PCA components fit the systematic structures out of the residual explicitly, while a regularised covariance down-weights the remaining correlated noise. Classical DOAS, covariance-weighted DOAS, and PCA-DOAS emerge as limiting cases of XDOAS. The algorithm is applied to the retrieval of OClO slant column densities from TROPOMI/S5P, a weak absorber measured at large solar zenith angles where the residual structures are most pronounced. Evaluated against the three reference retrievals on TROPOMI measurements using identical fit parameters, XDOAS reaches the precision of the best advanced retrievals while being the only one that also gives an uncertainty consistent with the spectral fit quality of each pixel. A consistency test between the RMS residual and the retrieval uncertainty separates the four retrievals, covariance-weighted DOAS gives uncertainties that are decoupled from the residual (R2 = 0.002), PCA-DOAS gives uncertainties that are fixed to the residual because the PCA components fit out part of the random noise (R2 = 0.991), and XDOAS is the only retrieval whose uncertainty follows the spectral fit quality of each pixel with a moderate pixel-to-pixel spread (R2 = 0.977). The comparison against the S5P-PAL OClO product based on empirical post-processed DOAS retrieval, shows close agreement (R2 = 0.922). Where the OClO signal is strong, over the polar vortex, the two products agree almost exactly (slope 1.02, R2 = 0.946), while XDOAS gives a lower RMS residual and a smoother uncertainty field specially, most of all under the low-illumination conditions in which OClO is measured. XDOAS is the baseline algorithm for the operational OClO product of the Copernicus Sentinel-5 mission from the EUMETSAT AC-SAF. XDOAS is a general framework that can be applied to any trace gas with narrow absorption bands, and in particular to measurements under extrema viewing conditions typically in geostationary missions like Sentinel-4, GEMS, and TEMPO.

title: METAVERSE TEKNOLOJİLERİNİN EĞİTİMDE ETKİN KULLANIMINA YÖNELİK BİR MODEL TASARIMI VE PROTOTİP UYGULAMASI
source: Journal of Business in The Digital Age
summary: Çalışmanın amacı, uzaktan eğitim platformlarında etkileşimi ve kullanıcı katılımını destekleyebilecek metaverse teknolojilerine dayalı bir eğitim prototipi geliştirmek ve bu prototipin pilot uygulama üzerinden kullanım sürecini değerlendirm
content: Çalışmanın amacı, uzaktan eğitim platformlarında etkileşimi ve kullanıcı katılımını destekleyebilecek metaverse teknolojilerine dayalı bir eğitim prototipi geliştirmek ve bu prototipin pilot uygulama üzerinden kullanım sürecini değerlendirmektir. Çalışma, kavramsal tasarım, platform seçimi, teknik altyapı kararları, kullanım senaryoları, pilot ders uygulamaları ve ölçme-değerlendirme planlarını bütünleştiren tasarım tabanlı bir araştırma yaklaşımıyla yapılandırılmıştır. Geliştirme sürecinde sürdürülebilir bir platform oluşturmak amacıyla cihaz uyumluluğu, içerik zenginliği ve senkron/asenkron kullanım kapasitesi dikkate alınarak Engage VR altyapısı tercih edilmiştir. Prototip; eğitmenin üç boyutlu nesne, video, belge ve dinamik tahta kullanabildiği; öğrencilerin avatar temelli etkileşim, grup çalışması, tartışma ve sonradan erişim senaryolarıyla sisteme katılabildiği bütünleşik bir sanal sınıf altyapısı olarak tasarlanmıştır. Prototip uygulamanın ilk örneği bir ders üzerinden gerçekleştirilmiş, üç boyutlu öğrenme nesneleri, sahne sunumları ve eşzamanlı etkileşimli etkinlikler test edilmiştir. Pilot uygulamadan elde edilen ön bulgular, VR ortamının klasik çevrim içi derslere kıyasla öğrencilerin çevrim içi öğrenme ortamına katılımı, derse odaklanması ve öğrenme sürecine aktif dahil olması açısından olumlu bir potansiyel taşıdığına işaret etmektedir. Bununla birlikte teknik sürdürülebilirlik, içerik geliştirme maliyeti ve kullanıcı deneyimi gibi boyutların dikkatle yönetilmesi gerektiği değerlendirilmiştir. Çalışma sonunda metaverse destekli uzaktan eğitim için bir prototip mimarisi, uygulama bileşenleri ve pilot kullanım sürecine yönelik ön değerlendirme yaklaşımı önerilmiştir.

title: Assessing planning-reference electrification envelopes against a calibrated EV-diffusion trajectory in Puerto Rico
summary: Abstract Transportation–electrification pathways are increasingly used as inputs for long-term infrastructure and energy-planning decisions. In Puerto Rico, legislative, regulatory, and planning instruments provide context for transportatio
content: Abstract Transportation–electrification pathways are increasingly used as inputs for long-term infrastructure and energy-planning decisions. In Puerto Rico, legislative, regulatory, and planning instruments provide context for transportation electrification and decarbonization through mid-century; however, they do not prescribe a unique temporal pathway for electrification of the reference vehicle fleet. This paper develops a consistency-assessment framework that compares planning-reference electrification envelopes, informed by Puerto Rico’s policy and decarbonization context, with a generalized-logistic trajectory calibrated from historical registered EV-stock observations. Historical registered EV-stock data from $$2014$$ through $$2023$$ are used to calibrate the generalized-logistic model, while front-loaded, linear, and delayed electrification envelopes are constructed around a common reference planning endpoint. The resulting pathways are compared using an adoption-level discrepancy metric, $$\Delta P(t)$$ , and a transition-time discrepancy metric, $$\Delta T_x$$ , which quantify differences in electrification levels and milestone-attainment timing, respectively. The calibrated model reproduces the observed series with $$R^{2}=0.996$$ on cumulative stock and $$R^{2}=0.959$$ on annual increments, and parameter uncertainty is propagated to both metrics by profile likelihood and residual bootstrap. Under the $$100\%$$ reference endpoint, the calibrated trajectory remains below the three primary planning-reference envelopes at the representative planning years evaluated. Relative to the common $$2050$$ planning benchmark, the benchmark-to-model adoption-level discrepancy reaches approximately $$25$$ percentage points ( $$95\%$$ interval $$22$$ to $$30$$ ). Representative electrification milestones are attained approximately $$2$$ to $$19$$ years later than under the corresponding envelopes, with delays of approximately $$11$$ to $$16$$ years at the $$90\%$$ electrification milestone; under the $$100\%$$ reference endpoint, the base-case discrepancies for the three primary envelopes remain positive across the bootstrap replicates evaluated. These results illustrate how differences between planning assumptions and a calibrated diffusion trajectory may affect charging-demand projections, infrastructure-deployment schedules, and long-term power-system planning; they are not deterministic forecasts or assessments of policy compliance. Sensitivity analyses across the reference endpoint, the saturation reference, the power-law envelope shape, and a sigmoid-family robustness check show that the reported discrepancy is governed primarily by endpoint and temporal-shape assumptions, with a break-even endpoint near $$75\%$$ , whereas the saturation reference has a comparatively small effect on normalized adoption-level and transition-time metrics but materially affects absolute plug-in-equivalent charging-energy estimates.
