To reclaim lost territories due to foreign aggressions in the colonial period, successive Chinese governments have pursued both diplomatic negotiations, as seen with Myanmar and Nepal, and more assertive measures with India and Southeast Asian countries. This study employs a qualitative research methodology with the help of archival methods within the constructivist theory and explicates China preference formation, specifically focused on Ladakh and Aksai Chin.

title: Pragmatic data-driven AI-based approach for exploring the effects of important constructs on flight cancellations in disruptions and infectious diseases
source: European journal of tourism, hospitality and recreation
summary: Abstract This study presents a pragmatic real-world approach for exploring flight cancellations in disrupted situations and infectious diseases. The airline industry has been prone to disruptions, and a huge number of flight cancellations h
content: Abstract This study presents a pragmatic real-world approach for exploring flight cancellations in disrupted situations and infectious diseases. The airline industry has been prone to disruptions, and a huge number of flight cancellations have been reported in recent years. In this study, an AI-based, data-driven approach is used to explore flight cancellation patterns in the wake of disruption. The correct flight information is important to save time, money and resources for airline customers. Data pertaining to the event of flight cancellation in disruption has not been properly presented in previous studies. Thus, in this study, the prediction power of artificial intelligence tools has been exploited for flight cancellations. Artificial intelligence tools, namely two-class neural network regression, two-class decision forest, a two-class locally deep support vector machine, and two-class logistic regression, were utilized for prediction. The precision, accuracy and recall performances of all the methods used are 100%. The confusion matrix depicts that all four methods correctly predict the outcome of flight cancellation. For the total of 549169 tested flights, 549168 flights have been correctly predicted. The only false positive instance shows that there is only one case where the flight was not canceled, but the methods incorrectly predicted it as canceled. Thus, for almost all the cases, the predictions are correct. The correlation calculated from the huge data of 2745847 flights reveals that flight cancellations have a frail positive relation with departure and arrival delays. Moreover, there is a fragile negative relationship with airtime, weather delay, carrier delay, security delay, NAS delay, and late aircraft delay. The lessons learned from planning and coping with disruptions can be used as preemptive preparation guidelines for handling emergency situations in the future.

title: Glocalising pedagogy in a bicultural and multilingual school ecology: professional legitimacy and identity negotiation among transnational novice Chinese language teachers in Aotearoa New Zealand
source: Journal of Multilingual and Multicultural Development
summary: As language teachers increasingly move across countries, they need to negotiate the relationship between global professional knowledge and local educational and cultural demands. Yet little is known about how transnational novice language t
content: As language teachers increasingly move across countries, they need to negotiate the relationship between global professional knowledge and local educational and cultural demands. Yet little is known about how transnational novice language teachers experience glocalisation over time, particularly when gaining professional recognition requires them to engage with unfamiliar local cultural expectations and ways of knowing. This study examined how transnational novice Chinese language teachers experienced and negotiated glocalisation within a bicultural and multilingual school ecology in Aotearoa New Zealand, and how this process shaped their professional legitimacy and teacher identity. It drew on longitudinal data, including reflective journals and interviews over 8 months, and analysed them through an abductive qualitative longitudinal approach. Findings show that glocalisation developed through a gradual process of local becoming. Participants first entered the local school world through everyday and Māori cultural practices, gradually recognising the limits of their prior knowledge and adapting Chinese teaching to locally meaningful practices and learner contexts. Over time, these experiences strengthened local professional recognition and reshaped how participants understood themselves as teachers. In addition, the professional capital gained through glocalisation may not travel easily across contexts but may depend on how it is reinterpreted and revalued in future settings.

title: Ethnographies of Human‐AI Collaborations: What Arrangements of Expertise Emerge?
summary: ABSTRACT In this review, I outline four arrangements on the spectrum of human experts‐AI collaboration, as studied from an ethnographic, grounded perspective by sociology, management, and STS scholars. Starting with the sociology of experti
content: ABSTRACT In this review, I outline four arrangements on the spectrum of human experts‐AI collaboration, as studied from an ethnographic, grounded perspective by sociology, management, and STS scholars. Starting with the sociology of expertise's definitions of what constitutes “expert work,” I first review cases in which AI almost replaced human expertise, those in which AI aims for ‘no human in the loop,’ offering reasons why such complete automation has not succeeded. Second, I review cases where AI is a bit ‘too much’ and becomes exploitive and bossy, where most sociological research is focused, that is, algorithmic management, platform and gig economies, surveillance capitalism, and digital labor. Third, I review cases where AI offers new opportunities for expertise to develop new markets, roles, and co‐productions, and while incurring some professional risks for myself, I title these cases as ‘yay.’ And last, I review cases where ethnographic, grounded studies have shown that experts simply ignore or dismiss AI, with a simple ‘ nah .’ While differentiating these four points on the continuum of human‐AI collaboration, I discuss how the study of AI is entangled with the study of expertise in the 21st century, highlight questions and agendas, and offer directions for future research.

title: Big Brother or Good Steward? Earnings Management and the Disclosure of Personal Data Protection Systems
summary: Using a sample of Chinese listed firms from 2009 to 2024, we examine whether voluntary disclosure of personal data protection systems (PDPS) is associated with earnings management. We document a moral licensing effect; that is, firms with h
content: Using a sample of Chinese listed firms from 2009 to 2024, we examine whether voluntary disclosure of personal data protection systems (PDPS) is associated with earnings management. We document a moral licensing effect; that is, firms with higher PDPS disclosure engage in more real earnings management (REM). Specifically, a one‐standard‐deviation increase in PDPS disclosure is associated with a 21.5% increase in REM relative to its absolute mean, while accrual‐based earnings management (AEM) remains statistically unaffected. Decomposing REM reveals that abnormal production costs account for the overall increase, whereas discretionary expenses and abnormal operating cash flows exhibit offsetting patterns. Mechanism analyses suggest that the moral licensing conferred by PDPS disclosure facilitates opportunistic operational decisions through heightened operational risk under compliance pressure and weakened external monitoring reflected in lower audit quality. Cross‐sectional tests further indicate that this licensing effect is attenuated in firms embedded in stronger Confucian cultures, without political connections, and with more stable executive leadership. Overall, this study extends research on the determinants of earnings management from the perspective of data governance. We also enrich understanding of the economic consequences of voluntary PDPS disclosure. Our findings caution that disclosure of data protection practices may generate unintended governance consequences by enabling value‐destroying operational manipulation. The lesson is clear: in a world shaped by data and moral perception, voluntary disclosure is not always the cure; it can just as easily become the cover.

title: A meta-ethnography of staff experiences of raising concerns about quality and safety in residential aged care
summary: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Speaking up about quality and safety issues can protect older people and support learning in health and social care systems. In aged care, staff work in diverse roles to deliver care to residents with complex care
content: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Speaking up about quality and safety issues can protect older people and support learning in health and social care systems. In aged care, staff work in diverse roles to deliver care to residents with complex care needs. This meta-ethnography aimed to synthesise evidence on staff experiences of raising concerns about quality and safety in long-term residential aged care. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We included qualitative studies examining staff experiences of speaking up, incident reporting, and whistleblowing. Five databases were searched. The seven phases of meta-ethnography were used to translate first and second order constructs into third order constructs and a line-of-argument synthesis. RESULTS: Thirteen articles of 11 studies were synthesised to reveal four third order constructs: 1. Sensemaking a concern, 2. Organisational cultures determine how they are voiced, heard and respond to, 3. Systemic resources shape and constrain possibilities for voicing, and 4. Normalisation of poor care and loss of moral agency in organisations that respond with indifference. Raising concerns was a dynamic, recursive process encompassing phases of recognising, voicing, and organisational responding. Where quality and safety issues were normalised, individualised, or met with limited action, staff described moral distress, disengagement, and, in some cases, exit from the organisation or sector. DISCUSSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Raising concerns in residential aged care is a dynamic process shaped by interrelated individual, organisational and systemic factors. Speaking up interventions need to go beyond skills training to address phases of recognising care quality issues and how organisations respond when they are raised.

title: Oxidizer temperature effect on the modes of ignition of wood biomass particles
source: Bulletin of the Tomsk Polytechnic University Geo Assets Engineering
summary: In 2022–2024, it was officially established that unconventional renewable energy sources (wind turbines and solar panels) in the foreseeable future (15–20 years) will not be able to replace traditional energy (thermal and nuclear power plan
content: In 2022–2024, it was officially established that unconventional renewable energy sources (wind turbines and solar panels) in the foreseeable future (15–20 years) will not be able to replace traditional energy (thermal and nuclear power plants) due to the lack of powerful, reliable and safe electric energy storage systems. Therefore, coal-fired power plants in the coming decades will certainly generate large amounts of electricity not only in China, India, the USA and Poland, but also in many other countries. In this regard, the world-class scientific problem is environmental pollution by coal combustion products (flue gases from coal-fired power plants). This problem can be solved by burning coal in the furnaces of steam and hot water boilers mixed with biomass (wood in the first place). But wood burning in the furnaces of boiler installations so far in most real technologies leads to intensive slagging of heating surfaces. Therefore, an urgent task, the solution of which can ensure the transition to environmentally friendly and resource-saving coal-fired power in the future, is the task of substantiating the parameters of ignition and combustion of wood biomass particles. Aim. To determine the combustion modes of wood biomass particles of different sizes during high-temperature heating. Object. Wood particles (pine) of cubic shape of three characteristic sizes. Method. To determine the ignition and combustion modes of cubic wood particles under high-temperature heating conditions, a special experimental setup with laser illumination was used. Results. A conventional temperature boundary of Tcr=908 K was established for the transition between two ignition modes (gas-phase and heterogeneous) for pine wood biomass particles. It was also shown that the characteristic particle size of the wood (in the studied size range, L=4–8 mm) has no significant effect on the characteristics and conditions of the transition from one ignition mode to another. It was also experimentally established that, at relatively low oxidizer temperatures, the difference in ignition delay times for different ignition modes with a characteristic particle size of L=8 mm can reach 10%. For citation: Baranova (Kostoreva) A.A., Syrodoy S.V., Solodovnikova (Kostoreva) Zh.A., Omarov A.A., Nekrasov S.S., Senchikhin D.K. Oxidizer temperature effect on the modes of ignition of wood biomass particles. Bulletin of the Tomsk Polytechnic University. Geo Assets Engineering, 2026, vol. 337, no. 8, pp. 32–44. http://doi.org/10.18799/24131830/2026/8/5436

title: The Continuity and Rupture of the ‘New Washington Consensus’: From Biden to Trump 2.0
summary: ABSTRACT The ‘New Washington Consensus’ (NWC) represents a major intellectual shift in the US approach to global economic governance. However, the NWC has never been subject to systematic academic critique. With Trump's return to the White
content: ABSTRACT The ‘New Washington Consensus’ (NWC) represents a major intellectual shift in the US approach to global economic governance. However, the NWC has never been subject to systematic academic critique. With Trump's return to the White House ushering in a new era of US trade policy, the NWC is widely considered to be politically irrelevant in the existing literature. This article provides one of the first sustained critical assessments of the NWC and its legacy for the future of the international economic order. In particular, it argues that, contrary to prevailing assumptions, it is too early to dismiss the NWC as intellectually defunct. Although some elements of the NWC have been criticised and subsequently discarded in the Trump 2.0 era, the NWC nonetheless established the intellectual framework for Trump 2.0's trade statecraft. Therefore, a more rigorous engagement with the NWC and its evolving legacy provides a useful lens for imagining the future of the international economic order.

title: School well-being and student engagement among university students: The mediating role of growth mindset
summary: Student engagement is a key determinant of academic achievement in higher education. This study examined whether growth mindset mediates the relationship between school well-being and student engagement among university students. A cross-se
content: Student engagement is a key determinant of academic achievement in higher education. This study examined whether growth mindset mediates the relationship between school well-being and student engagement among university students. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with university students in Purwokerto, Indonesia, using standardized measures of school well-being, growth mindset, and student engagement. Mediation analysis was performed using Jamovi with bootstrapped confidence intervals. The findings showed that school well-being was positively associated with growth mindset, which in turn was positively associated with student engagement. Growth mindset significantly mediated the relationship between school well-being and student engagement, while the direct relationship between school well-being and student engagement was not significant. These findings suggest that growth mindset serves as an important psychological mechanism linking school well-being with student engagement. Supportive learning environments that foster both well-being and adaptive cognitive beliefs may therefore promote greater student engagement in higher education.

title: Örgütlerde Sürdürülebilir Davranışa Giden Psikolojik Yollar: Psikolojik Sahiplenme ve Yeşil Tutku
summary: Sürdürülebilir davranış, çevrenin korunması ve doğal kaynakların dengeli kullanımı açısından stratejik öneme sahiptir; ancak bu davranışların hangi psikolojik mekanizmalarla kalıcı olduğu konusunda literatür, psikolojik sahiplenme ve yeşil
content: Sürdürülebilir davranış, çevrenin korunması ve doğal kaynakların dengeli kullanımı açısından stratejik öneme sahiptir; ancak bu davranışların hangi psikolojik mekanizmalarla kalıcı olduğu konusunda literatür, psikolojik sahiplenme ve yeşil tutkuyu çoğunlukla birbirinden ayrı ayrı ele almıştır. Bu kavramsal çalışma, öz-belirleme kuramı (ÖBK) çerçevesinde özerklik, yeterlik ve ilişkililik ihtiyaçlarının doyumunun, sürdürülebilir davranışın iki kritik bileşeni olan psikolojik sahiplenme ve yeşil tutkuyu nasıl besleyebileceğini bütünleşik bir modelle açıklamaktadır. Psikolojik sahiplenme, çevresel hedefleri sahiplenme ve sorumluluk almayı; yeşil tutku çevresel değerlere yönelik duygusal enerji ve gönüllü katılımı artırarak sürdürülebilir davranışın motivasyonel temelini pekiştirmektedir. Çalışmanın özgün katkısı, bu iki yapıyı birlikte ele alarak sürdürülebilir davranışın psikolojik dinamiklerle güçlendiğini gösteren açıklayıcı bir çerçeve sunmasıdır. Bu çerçeve, farklı sektör ve kültürlerde ampirik sınamalar, aracı veya düzenleyici değişkenlerin test edilmesi ve boylamsal tasarımlarla süreç dinamiklerinin incelenmesi için somut bir araştırma gündemi önermektedir. Model, uygulayıcılar açısından ise sürdürülebilir davranışların geliştirilmesinde yalnızca farkındalık ve teşviklere değil, çalışanların katılımını, otonomisini ve anlamlı katkı fırsatlarını artırarak sahiplenme ve yeşil tutkuyu birlikte besleyen insan kaynakları ve liderlik uygulamalarına odaklanılması gerektiğine işaret etmektedir.

title: Academic burnout among female adolescents: A resource-based model of social support, perfectionism, and academic self-efficacy
summary: Academic burnout is an increasingly recognized psychosocial challenge among adolescents exposed to sustained academic demands. Guided by Conservation of Resources theory, this study develops and tests a resource-based model examining how so
content: Academic burnout is an increasingly recognized psychosocial challenge among adolescents exposed to sustained academic demands. Guided by Conservation of Resources theory, this study develops and tests a resource-based model examining how social support and perfectionism are associated with academic burnout through academic self-efficacy among female upper secondary students. Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 522 students aged 15–18 years in metropolitan Thailand and analyzed using structural equation modeling. Academic self-efficacy was negatively associated with burnout, whereas both adaptive and socially prescribed perfectionism were positively related to burnout. Adaptive perfectionism was positively associated with self-efficacy, while socially prescribed perfectionism showed no direct association. Family support was indirectly associated with lower burnout through self-efficacy, whereas teacher emotional support demonstrated a direct negative association with burnout. Mediation analyses indicated that academic self-efficacy partially explained the relationships between adaptive perfectionism, family support, and burnout. Overall, the findings extend Conservation of Resources theory by highlighting how interactions between internal psychological resources and external social resources shape burnout processes among female adolescents in high-pressure educational contexts. The study contributes to interdisciplinary social science research by providing gender-sensitive insights into adolescent well-being and informing resource-focused prevention strategies.

title: Strategic human resource management, leadership, and governance practices in a university hospital: a qualitative study of healthcare managers’ experiences
summary: Strategic human resource management, leadership, and governance are recognized as complementary management processes that play a fundamental role in enhancing organizational effectiveness and improving the quality of healthcare services. Ho
content: Strategic human resource management, leadership, and governance are recognized as complementary management processes that play a fundamental role in enhancing organizational effectiveness and improving the quality of healthcare services. However, translating these processes into practice is often challenged by competing organizational priorities, structural constraints, and limited resources. This qualitative study, drawing on the experiences of physicians, nurses, and administrative managers working in a public university hospital, aims to examine how strategic human resource management and leadership practices are carried out, how these practices reflect in employee engagement and performance, the main challenges encountered during implementation, and how misalignments between policy and everyday practice are managed. Additionally, managerial strategies developed to support motivation and sustainable performance are interpreted through a qualitative lens. Data were collected through semi-structured, in-depth interviews with purposively sampled managers, and the data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis approach. The study's reporting aligned with COREQ guidelines developed for qualitative interview research. The analysis identified six interrelated themes: (i) competency-based planning, training and development, and quality-oriented strategic HRM practices; (ii) relational leadership, role modeling, and trust building; (iii) fairness, transparency, and accountability in governance processes, along with policy-practice misalignments; (iv) staff shortages, increasing workload, and the risk of burnout; (v) managerial strategies supporting motivation and employee engagement; and (vi) local adaptation and innovative solution practices developed under structural constraints. The findings indicate that balancing institutional performance targets with workforce capacity cannot be achieved solely through technical planning tools; rather, the sustainability of this balance depends critically on fair and transparent governance mechanisms that are perceived as legitimate by frontline staff. The study contributes qualitative evidence to ongoing discussions on the integrated consideration of strategic HRM, leadership, and governance processes and aims to offer analytical insights to inform policy development and institutional improvement efforts in healthcare organizations.

title: Infidelity, Emotional Abuse, and Domestic Violence as Predictors of Marital Dissolution Among Married Couples in Delta North Senatorial District, Delta State, Nigeria.
source: RADINKA JOURNAL OF SCIENCE AND SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
summary: This study investigated adultery, emotional abuse, and domestic violence as key predictors of divorce, driven by the rising prevalence of marital instability and the need to comprehend the combined impact of relational stressors within the
content: This study investigated adultery, emotional abuse, and domestic violence as key predictors of divorce, driven by the rising prevalence of marital instability and the need to comprehend the combined impact of relational stressors within the Nigerian sociocultural context. Utilizing a quantitative descriptive survey design, the population comprised married men and women in the study area, with a sample size of 392 respondents determined using the Taro Yamane formula via a multi-stage sampling technique. Data were gathered using a validated instrument entitled the Infidelity, Emotional Abuse, Domestic Violence, and Marital Dissolution Questionnaire (IEDVMDQ), which demonstrated high internal consistency with a Cronbach’s alpha coefficient greater than 0.70. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics for descriptive statistics (mean and standard deviation) and inferential statistics at a significance level of 0.05. The results revealed that all variables exceeded the criterion mean of, indicating that infidelity (aggregate mean = ), emotional abuse (aggregate mean = ), and domestic violence (aggregate mean = ) significantly impact marital breakdown. Domestic violence emerged as the strongest predictor, followed by emotional abuse and adultery, while the combined effect of these factors substantially predicted marital dissolution among married couples. These findings underscore the multifaceted nature of marital instability and the critical need for coordinated therapeutic strategies. The study concludes that adultery, emotional abuse, and domestic violence are deeply intertwined factors driving marriage breakup in the Delta North Senatorial District, thereby recommending the implementation of targeted counseling programs, public awareness campaigns, and robust policy measures.

title: The Effect of Schema Therapy on Aggressive Behaviour among Senior Secondary School Students in Oyo State, Nigeria
source: International Journal of Counseling and Psychotherapy
summary: Background: Pervasive aggressive behavior in secondary schools severely undermines school safety, yet conventional school guidance rarely addresses the underlying early maladaptive schemas. Objective: This study aims to investigate the effe
content: Background: Pervasive aggressive behavior in secondary schools severely undermines school safety, yet conventional school guidance rarely addresses the underlying early maladaptive schemas. Objective: This study aims to investigate the effect of Schema Therapy on aggressive behavior among senior secondary school students in Oyo State, Nigeria. Methods: A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design was employed, involving 116 Senior Secondary School II students with high aggression scores recruited via multistage sampling. The experimental group received a ten-week structured Schema Therapy protocol, while the control group received conventional counseling. Data were collected using the Aggressive Behaviour Questionnaire (α = 0.89) and analyzed using Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) at the .05 level. Results: Schema Therapy produced a statistically significant main effect in reducing student aggression compared to conventional counseling. Gender also had a significant main effect, with female students recording higher post-test aggression scores than males. No significant treatment-by-gender interaction occurred, demonstrating consistent therapeutic gains across participants. Conclusion: Schema Therapy is empirically superior to conventional guidance in reducing adolescent aggression regardless of gender. Originality/Value: This study brings scientific novelty to the field of counseling and psychotherapy by uncovering the efficacy of Schema Therapy in restructuring early maladaptive schemas within a non-Western educational context that has remained underexplored. These findings enrich empirical evidence while providing a strategic reference for school counselors and policymakers in developing sustainable interventions.

title: The effect of proactive personality on professional commitment through career mindfulness in tour guidance students
summary: This study examines the mediating role of career mindfulness (CM) in the relationship between proactive personality (PP) and professional commitment (PC) among Turkish undergraduate students aiming for a career in tour guiding. Despite the
content: This study examines the mediating role of career mindfulness (CM) in the relationship between proactive personality (PP) and professional commitment (PC) among Turkish undergraduate students aiming for a career in tour guiding. Despite the importance of PP and mindfulness in career success, previous studies have not tested this relationship using the CM scale. Data collected from 592 students via online and face-to-face surveys between 1 November and 20 December 2023 were analyzed using structural equation modelling within the mediation framework. The findings revealed that PP did not have a direct significant effect on PC; however, PP positively predicted CM, and CM significantly increased PC. The results indicate that the effect of personality tendencies on professional attitudes can be mediated by career-focused self-regulation processes, such as CM, in the context of tour guiding. By integrating CM into the career development literature, the study contributes to personality–attitude relationships in a mechanism-based manner and generates implications for education and industry practice.

title: Scalable isolation of soil genomic DNA from microbial eukaryotes to multicellular micro‑ and mesofauna
summary: Global initiatives emphasise the need for harmonised soil biodiversity assessments. Efficient DNA extraction methods that accommodate larger soil volumes are essential for capturing organisms at higher trophic levels than bacteria and fungi
content: Global initiatives emphasise the need for harmonised soil biodiversity assessments. Efficient DNA extraction methods that accommodate larger soil volumes are essential for capturing organisms at higher trophic levels than bacteria and fungi and for supporting extensive sampling campaigns. We developed and evaluated a scalable, cost-efficient, and automation-ready soil DNA isolation protocol and compared its performance with two widely used commercial extraction methods: Qiagen DNeasy PowerSoil Pro (0.25 g soil input) and Qiagen DNeasy PowerMax Soil (2.5 g soil input). Four contrasting soil types representing agricultural and forest ecosystems (mull, sandy till, peat, and coarse mineral soil) were analysed. The new protocol combines bead-beating in sodium thiocyanate lysis buffer with either silica-membrane or carboxyl-coated magnetic bead purification and was tested using soil inputs of 2.5 g and 5 g for one soil type. DNA extracts were sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq platform using universal eukaryotic 18S rRNA gene primers to characterise soil metazoans and microbial eukaryotes. The developed protocol, combining a tenfold increase in soil input with commercial kit purification, produced the highest DNA yields in three of four soil types, increasing DNA recovery by up to 2.3-fold compared with the commercial maxiprep method. It also consistently detected the greatest metazoan richness, recovering up to 103% more taxa than the conventional miniprep method and up to 82% more taxa than the commercial maxiprep method. The carboxyl-coated magnetic bead workflow also performed well, recovering up to 83% more metazoan taxa than the miniprep method and up to 55% more taxa than the maxiprep method, particularly in forest soils. For microbial eukaryotes and protists, the commercial maxiprep and combination of developed high lysis volume and commercial kit silica purification protocols generally yielded the highest richness in agricultural soils, whereas the developed protocol performed best in coarse xeric forest soils. These results indicate that at least a tenfold increase in soil input relative to conventional 0.25 g extractions is required for reliable characterisation of mesofauna diversity, while further increases may provide additional gains. The developed DNA isolation protocol offers a solution for large-scale soil biodiversity assessments, supporting the integration of higher trophic levels into eDNA-based monitoring frameworks and future soil health monitoring programmes.

title: AI-based models for risks of work-related musculoskeletal disorders in office workers: exploring generalisability, interpretability and use of binary scales
summary: Artificial intelligence has the potential to enhance risk assessment of work-related musculoskeletal disorders in office environments. This study externally validated previously developed machine learning models and evaluated the performanc
content: Artificial intelligence has the potential to enhance risk assessment of work-related musculoskeletal disorders in office environments. This study externally validated previously developed machine learning models and evaluated the performance of simplified binary data inputs. Six models trained on data from 810 office workers were validated using an independent dataset of 74 globally recruited participants. Model performance across nine anatomical regions was assessed using F1-scores and AUC-ROC metrics. SHapley Additive exPlanations were used to interpret risk factor contributions, and model performance using ordinal Likert-scale inputs was compared with binary-transformed representations. Generalisability varied by anatomical region, with moderate performance for high-prevalence regions (neck and lower back) and reduced accuracy for low-prevalence regions. XGB showed moderate but comparatively stable performance across several anatomical regions. These findings highlight the need for region-specific validation and support the feasibility of simplified, interpretable, and scalable AI-based tools for practical ergonomic risk assessment in office environments.

title: GIS-based flood risk assessment in the Zhabay River Basin, Kazakhstan
summary: Flooding is one of the most damaging natural hazards in the steppe regions of northern Kazakhstan, where rapid spring snowmelt frequently causes severe inundation. In the Zhabay River basin, recent flood events have led to significant socio
content: Flooding is one of the most damaging natural hazards in the steppe regions of northern Kazakhstan, where rapid spring snowmelt frequently causes severe inundation. In the Zhabay River basin, recent flood events have led to significant socio-economic losses in Atbasar and nearby settlements. Despite their recurrence, spatially explicit flood risk assessments for this basin remain limited. To address this gap, the present study develops an integrated GIS-based framework that combines flood hazard assessment, vulnerability analysis, inundation scenario modeling, and satellite-based validation for comprehensive flood risk assessment. Flood hazard was assessed using indicators representing both basin susceptibility and hydrometeorological conditions controlling flood generation. Indicator weights were derived using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). Flood vulnerability was assessed using socio-economic and environmental vulnerability indicators. Integration of hazard and vulnerability layers enabled the development of a spatial flood risk model. Model performance was evaluated against observed flood extents derived from Sentinel-2 imagery using the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) for flood events. Model validation using ROC analysis demonstrated good to excellent predictive performance, with AUC values of 0.920, 0.820, and 0.906 for the 2017, 2019, and 2024 flood events, respectively. The proposed framework provides a basis for flood risk management and disaster risk reduction in snow-fed river basins. The main novelty of the study lies in the integration of hydrometeorological flood-triggering factors, spatial vulnerability indicators, inundation scenario modeling, and satellite-based validation within a unified GIS framework, providing a transferable approach for flood risk assessment in data-scarce snow-fed river basins.

title: TEACHERS’ WORK BELIEFS AMONG PUBLIC SECONDARY TEACHERS IN ISABELA
source: International Journal of Education Literacies and Curriculum Studies
summary: This study aimed to identify the profile of teacher-respondents, determine their work beliefs, and examine differences in these beliefs when grouped according to their profile. A descriptive-comparative design was utilized, involving 189 te
content: This study aimed to identify the profile of teacher-respondents, determine their work beliefs, and examine differences in these beliefs when grouped according to their profile. A descriptive-comparative design was utilized, involving 189 teachers who responded to a validated questionnaire. Data were analyzed using frequency counts, percentages, means, and t-tests. Findings revealed that most respondents were female, married, aged 26–30 years, held a bachelor’s degree with master’s units, and had 6–10 years of teaching experience. Teachers considered highly important work beliefs related to maintaining safe and well-equipped facilities, upholding professional dignity and ethical standards, fostering positive and fair learning environments, applying differentiated and responsive teaching strategies, supporting students’ competence development, and reflecting on the PPST standards. Significant differences in work beliefs were found when grouped according to age, civil status, educational attainment, and years of teaching experience, particularly in physical facilities, professional growth, interpersonal relationships, social environment, and new challenges. No significant differences were observed when grouped according to gender. Personal gratification was rated as most important. The findings highlight the need for improved school facilities, continuous professional development, and supportive work environments that address teachers’ diverse characteristics, while reinforcing learner-centered teaching practices.

title: Spatiotemporal trends and seasonal variations in meteorological parameters and radio refractivity across Nigeria’s eco-climatic zones
summary: The propagation of radio waves/signals is strongly influenced by atmospheric parameters, leading to signal degradation, unpredictable communication ranges, and link blackouts; however, this understanding has not been fully explored across d
content: The propagation of radio waves/signals is strongly influenced by atmospheric parameters, leading to signal degradation, unpredictable communication ranges, and link blackouts; however, this understanding has not been fully explored across diverse eco-climatic zones. Using meteorological data from selected locations across Nigeria’s eco-climatic zones from 1981 to 2022, this study assesses the impact of temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and precipitation on radio refractivity at annual and seasonal timescales (dry, onset, wet, and cessation periods). For the annual trend analysis, the Mann-Kendall trend test showed a noticeable increase in variability in both temperature and relative humidity. These trends were further supported by innovative trend analysis, which revealed a steady increase in refractivity, especially in humid climates like Yenagoa and Ibadan. For the analysis across seasons, positive refractivity deviations were largest and most consistent in both the wet and cessation periods, which mainly occurred over the humid and coastal areas (0.13 to 0.15 N-units/year), but weaker or negative trends were observed in the dry and onset periods in the Sahel and Sudan savannah (northern) locations (-0.236 to 0.224 N-units/year). Correlation analysis revealed strong relationships between refractivity and humidity, especially at Sahel and Sudan savannah sites ( r > 0.90). The multilinear regression-based sensitivity framework indicated that relative humidity exerted a greater influence on the refractivity in these climates than in the Mangrove and Freshwater zones; the reverse was identified for temperature. These findings have significant implications for Nigeria’s telecommunications industry and other tropical regions with comparable climatic characteristics, particularly for optimizing network planning and mitigating signal degradation caused by weather fluctuations.

title: Ta’dib-based Islamic Parenting Model as an Intervention Strategy for Developing Emotional Intelligence among Primary School Children: A Therapeutic Relational Approach
source: International Journal of Counseling and Psychotherapy
summary: Background: Children’s emotional intelligence is frequently addressed separately from spiritual-moral frameworks, leaving a critical conceptual gap regarding how Islamic educational philosophy functions as a relational therapeutic intervent
content: Background: Children’s emotional intelligence is frequently addressed separately from spiritual-moral frameworks, leaving a critical conceptual gap regarding how Islamic educational philosophy functions as a relational therapeutic intervention to optimize child socioemotional competence. Objective: This study aims to formulate a ta’dib-Based Islamic Parenting Model as an intervention strategy and therapeutic relational approach for developing emotional intelligence among primary school children. Methods: A Directed Qualitative Content Analysis design was employed, systematically analyzing classical Islamic educational texts alongside contemporary developmental psychology literature through a deductive categorization matrix encompassing foundational values, relational practices, therapeutic mechanisms, and emotional outcomes. Results: Children's emotional intelligence cannot be developed through verbal indoctrination or rigid punishment; rather, it is cultivated within a therapeutic relational ecology where moral guidance, parental emotional composure, and secure attachment integrate holistically. Conclusion: The ta’dib-based parenting model cultivates children’s emotional intelligence (self-awareness, emotional regulation, empathy, and social competence) through a therapeutic relational approach rather than unidirectional moral doctrine. This dynamic operates through parental modeling, the habituation of adab (ethical conduct), and secure attachment within the family. Originality/Value: This paper advances theoretical perspectives in Islamic education, family counseling, and developmental psychology by integrating ta’dib philosophy with contemporary therapeutic parenting to explain child socioemotional dynamics that have remained underexplored. The proposed conceptual framework serves as a strategic reference for family therapists, counselors, and educators in developing evidencebased parenting intervention programs.

title: Integrating Digital Games and Digital Tourism: Exploring Consumers’ Awareness of Chinese Heritage for Cultural Tourism
source: Journal of Games Game Art and Gamification
summary: Digital games have emerged as a significant platform for digital communication, extending beyond entertainment to include in-game advertising, brand communication, and cultural promotion. In recent years, the integration of gaming and touri
content: Digital games have emerged as a significant platform for digital communication, extending beyond entertainment to include in-game advertising, brand communication, and cultural promotion. In recent years, the integration of gaming and tourism has created new opportunities for cultural and heritage tourism marketing, enabling destinations to reach global audiences through immersive digital experiences. This study employs the Chinese action role-playing game Black Myth: Wukong as a case study to examine the potential of In-game Cultural Communication (ICC). Specifically, the research investigates three key dimensions: (1) the revitalization and reinterpretation of traditional mythological characters, (2) the use of digital games as a medium for cultural communication and tourism promotion, and (3) the enhancement of cultural awareness and understanding among non-Chinese gamers. An exploratory qualitative research design was adopted, with data collected through a focus group comprising non-Chinese players familiar with the game. The findings indicate that the incorporation of Chinese mythology and cultural narratives contributes significantly to ICC by increasing players’ interest in Chinese culture and heritage. Furthermore, participants reported a greater awareness of cultural landmarks and traditions represented in the game, suggesting strong potential for promoting digital tourism experiences. The study highlights how games can serve as effective tools for cross-cultural communication, cultural preservation, and tourism marketing in an increasingly digital society.

title: Anemia prevalence and its association with dietary diversity, tea consumption, body mass index, and medical history among female university students in southern coastal Bangladesh
summary: Abstract Background Anemia is a significant public health concern among female university students in Bangladesh, and the situation may be worse in coastal areas due to socioeconomic and environmental factors. The purpose of this study was
content: Abstract Background Anemia is a significant public health concern among female university students in Bangladesh, and the situation may be worse in coastal areas due to socioeconomic and environmental factors. The purpose of this study was to assess the prevalence and associated factors of anemia among female students in southern coastal Bangladesh. Methods This cross-sectional study involved female students from two public universities in Bangladesh (Barishal Division). Data were collected using a self-administered structured questionnaire (completed on-site) covering sociodemographic, dietary, lifestyle, and medical history information. Anthropometric measurements were used to assess body mass index, and dietary diversity was evaluated using a nine-food group questionnaire (24-h recall method). Anemia was defined as hemoglobin < 12 g/dL (WHO criteria). Binary logistic regression models were used to determine factors associated with anemia. Results Out of 398 participants, 43.7% ( n = 174) had anemia. Underweight students were nearly twice more likely to be anemic compared to those with normal weight [adjusted odds ratio, AOR = 1.85, 95%CI = 1.10–3.11]. Drinking > 4 cups of tea/day was associated with higher odds of anemia than drinking no tea [AOR = 1.84, 95%CI = 1.06–3.18]. Participants with a history of iron deficiency anemia were significantly more likely to be anemic than those without the history [AOR = 1.72, 95%CI = 1.03–2.87]. Individuals with low dietary diversity were more likely to be anemic than those with high dietary diversity [AOR = 2.10, 95% CI 1.06–4.17]. Conclusions These findings support the need for campus-based screening and nutrition education. Further prospective research is needed to explore interventions among this demographic in Bangladesh.

title: POLICY BRIEF; Smart Agriculture as a Strategic Instrument for Reducing Urban–Rural Disparities in Land Use Efficiency in Kenya's Coast Region
summary: 1. Executive SummaryKenya's six coastal counties — Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi, Tana River, Lamu, and Taita-Taveta — exhibit a persistent and widening gap between the efficiency with which urban land is used (dense, high-value, infrastructure-se
content: 1. Executive SummaryKenya's six coastal counties — Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi, Tana River, Lamu, and Taita-Taveta — exhibit a persistent and widening gap between the efficiency with which urban land is used (dense, high-value, infrastructure-serviced) and the efficiency with which rural agricultural land is used (extensive, low-input, poorly serviced, and increasingly fragmented). This disparity undermines food security, drives unplanned rural-urban migration, and weakens the region's contribution to national and county development goals, including Vision 2030's economic pillar and the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda's agriculture value chain.Smart and digital agriculture — precision input management, mobile-based extension and market linkage, digital land and tenure records, remote-sensing-based land monitoring, and e-governance of agricultural value chains — offers a credible strategic lever for narrowing this gap without requiring rural land to replicate urban land-use intensity. The comparative and cross-country evidence base (including digital rural construction studies from China, smart territorial restructuring pilots in the EU, and Kenya's own mobile-money and e-extension experience) consistently associates digital agricultural transformation with improved land use efficiency, particularly where digital skills, tenure security, and market access improve together rather than in isolation.This brief argues that Kenya's coast region has the pre-conditions to convert this evidence into practice — mobile penetration, an active devolution architecture, and an existing inter-county coordination body (JKP) — but lacks a shared governance instrument to sequence and finance smart agriculture investment across counties. It proposes the Smart Agriculture Land-Use Convergence Framework (SALCF) as that instrument, structured around six pillars: digital land information and tenure; precision and climate-smart production technology; digital extension and market access; digital and physical infrastructure equity; county-level digital agriculture governance; and blended financing anchored in the existing Blue Finance Mobilisation Model (BFMM). The brief closes with a three-horizon implementation roadmap, an institutional map, an M&E framework built around a Land Use Efficiency Convergence Index, and risk mitigation measures.

title: Optimization of seeding density for maize grown in rainfed and irrigated systems
summary: The study aimed to evaluate the influence of maize seeding density on agronomic components and yield across two production environments: one irrigated and one rainfed. Two experiments were conducted using a randomized complete block design
content: The study aimed to evaluate the influence of maize seeding density on agronomic components and yield across two production environments: one irrigated and one rainfed. Two experiments were conducted using a randomized complete block design with five seeding densities (60, 75, 90, 105, and 120 thousand seeds ha⁻¹) and four replications, utilizing the DKB 230 VT PRO3 hybrid. Yield components and grain yield were analyzed, and the data were subjected to analysis of variance as well as linear and quadratic regression. The results showed a significant interaction between environment and density for most of the analyzed variables. Increasing density led to a reduction in several yield components, particularly in the rainfed environment, where ear length, hundred-grain weight, and the number of grains per ear decreased. In contrast, the irrigated environment exhibited greater stability in agronomic components and a higher capacity to support increased plant populations. The densities yielding the highest grain yield were 94.71 thousand seeds ha⁻¹ for the irrigated system and 82.19 thousand seeds ha⁻¹ for the rainfed system, demonstrating that density management should be adjusted according to the environment's water availability.

title: The Impact of Blue Economy Implementation on the Global Competitive Advantage of South Bali Fishermen: The Role of Sustainable Fisheries as a Mediating Variable
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of blue economy principles on the global competitive advantage of mud crab (Scylla spp.) fishers in the Tahura Ngurah Rai area, South Bali, with sustainable fisheries as a mediating variable, amid chall
content: This study aims to analyze the effect of blue economy principles on the global competitive advantage of mud crab (Scylla spp.) fishers in the Tahura Ngurah Rai area, South Bali, with sustainable fisheries as a mediating variable, amid challenges following the Benoa oil spill incident. This quantitative explanatory research involved 100 fishers selected through purposive sampling and analyzed using Partial Least Square Structural Equation Modeling (SEM- PLS). The results show that blue economy implementation has a significant positive effect on global competitive advantage, both directly (β=0.430; p<0.001) and indirectly through sustainable fisheries (indirect effect=0.204; p<0.001), which also acts as a partial mediator, explaining 52.2% of the variance in global competitive advantage. Importance- Performance Map analysis identifies capture operations, institutional integration, and biosecurity standards as priority areas for improvement. These findings underscore the importance of integrating blue economy and sustainable fisheries as a strategy to enhance the competitiveness of small- scale fishers in global markets.

title: Internship and Mentorship for Developing the Pedagogical Competence of Pre-Service Early Childhood Teachers: A Systematic Literature Review
source: International Journal of Learning Teaching and Educational Research
summary: The pedagogical competence of pre-service early childhood teachers develops not only through university coursework but also through guided participation in authentic settings. Yet internship and mentorship experiences remain uneven because
content: The pedagogical competence of pre-service early childhood teachers develops not only through university coursework but also through guided participation in authentic settings. Yet internship and mentorship experiences remain uneven because of persistent theory-practice disconnections, inconsistent mentoring, and insufficiently coherent practicum structures. This systematic literature review synthesised 37 peer-reviewed articles published from 2020 to 2025 and indexed in CNKI, Web of Science, and ERIC. Using a structured coding framework and thematic synthesis, the review examined study characteristics, theoretical orientations, processes of competence development, and the contextual conditions shaping those processes. Across the literature, pedagogical competence emerged as a multidimensional and situated capacity developed through classroom participation, mentoring, peer collaboration, and critical reflection. The effectiveness of these processes depended on institutional coordination, access to resources, mentor preparation and availability, academic support, manageable workloads, and a supportive school culture. Mentorship was especially important because it helped pre-service teachers interpret children's responses, connect theory with developmentally appropriate practice, and form a professional identity. The review therefore supports internship models that deliberately connect sustained classroom responsibility with prepared mentors, collaborative inquiry, and structured reflection. It also identifies design principles relevant to the further development and empirical evaluation of the Hengxing Internship Model. These findings offer a conceptual basis for teacher educators, institutions, and policymakers seeking context-responsive approaches to preparing reflective and adaptive early childhood teachers.

title: What Happens in Brussels Does Not Stay in Brussels
source: Slovak Yearbook of European Union Law
summary: This paper examines how the European Union (EU) addresses selected global challenges through its legal order, and the extent to which EU law achieves global reach beyond its territorial borders. Starting from the premise that global challen
content: This paper examines how the European Union (EU) addresses selected global challenges through its legal order, and the extent to which EU law achieves global reach beyond its territorial borders. Starting from the premise that global challenges must first be incorporated into “EU challenges,” the analysis explores how issues of global concern are brought within the scope of EU regulatory action through the competences conferred on the Union. The analysis focuses on selected regulatory responses in the fields of digital regulation, environmental protection and competition law, which serve as illustrative rather than exhaustive examples of how EU law addresses challenges of a global character. The paper further analyses the intention of the EU regulator when adopting such measures, distinguishing between expressed and non-expressed objectives of global regulation. It demonstrates that in certain cases—such as the GDPR, DSA, AI Act and EUDR—the intention to influence the behaviour of third-country actors is explicitly reflected in the recitals and provisions of the legislation, while in contrast, in instruments such as the DMA, EUTR and EU competition law, global effects arise implicitly from the protection and functioning of the internal market. In its second part, the paper identifies two principal mechanisms through which EU law achieves global reach. First, particular emphasis is placed on the de jure Brussels Effect, whereby third countries adopt or align with EU regulatory standards. Second, the extraterritorial reach of EU law, primarily through territorial extension, enables EU rules to apply to conduct with a sufficient connection to the internal market. In this context, the paper distinguishes between expressed and non-expressed extraterritoriality. It concludes that the EU operates as a global regulatory actor by shaping access to its internal market, positioning EU law as a benchmark for global standards.

title: Building Vocational High School Teacher Performance through the Synergy of Transformational Leadership, Organizational Culture, and Work Motivation in the Era of Vocational Education
summary: This study investigates the direct and indirect effects of principals’ transformational leadership, organizational culture, and work motivation on teacher performance in public vocational high schools (SMK) in Tebing Tinggi City. Employing
content: This study investigates the direct and indirect effects of principals’ transformational leadership, organizational culture, and work motivation on teacher performance in public vocational high schools (SMK) in Tebing Tinggi City. Employing a quantitative cross-sectional design with path analysis, data were collected from 153 teachers selected via proportional random sampling. Results reveal that organizational culture exerts the strongest direct influence on work motivation (77.8%), establishing it as the primary determinant of motivational climates. Work motivation functions as a critical amplifier, mediating the relationships between leadership/culture and teacher performance. Direct effects on performance are moderate: leadership (26.1%), culture (33.3%), and motivation (35.5%). However, indirect pathways through motivation yield substantially higher explanatory power (38.8% and 36.7%), with a simultaneous model accounting for 40.0% of performance variance. All hypothesized relationships are statistically significant, and the structural model demonstrates perfect fit. The findings challenge leadership-centric paradigms by highlighting organizational culture as the foundational driver of teacher motivation in vocational settings. Practically, the study advocates for integrated management strategies that prioritize culture-building, visionary leadership, and motivational interventions to sustain pedagogical excellence and enhance graduate workforce readiness in Industry 4.0.

title: Global Uncertainties and Income Disparities in Developing Countries
source: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries Social Science
summary: Background Income inequality has remained an important concern for social scientists since the 1980s. Global uncertainties profoundly exacerbate income disparities in developing countries, in addition to economic and institutional factors.
content: Background Income inequality has remained an important concern for social scientists since the 1980s. Global uncertainties profoundly exacerbate income disparities in developing countries, in addition to economic and institutional factors. This study investigates the relationship between world uncertainty and income inequality for a panel of 52 developing countries from 1996 to 2024. Method The study employs the Generalized Method of Moments to address endogeneity, unobserved heterogeneity, and dynamic panel data bias. The authors conducted a robustness analysis using the Two-Stage Least Squares method. Results The empirical findings reveal that an increase in world uncertainty widens income inequality in developing countries. Heightened uncertainty discourages new investments, slows economic activity, and disproportionately affects low-income groups. Moreover, an increase in GDP per capita enhances income inequality at early stages of development and then lowers it, providing evidence for the Kuznets curve. High inflation enhances income inequality, whereas the distributional impacts of official development assistance, human capital, and quality of institutions are favorable. These findings are robust to estimation methodology. Policy Recommendations The study suggests more effective crisis-management strategies to deal with income inequality during uncertain periods. The study also calls for increasing HC investments to reduce income inequality by raising wage income. Development aid may be an effective tool to mitigate INEQ.

title: Fear, power, and superintelligence: A realist reframing of AI catastrophic risk
summary: Debates on catastrophic artificial intelligence (AI) risk often frame artificial superintelligence as a problem of value alignment: the central task is to ensure that advanced systems act in accordance with human intentions or moral princip
content: Debates on catastrophic artificial intelligence (AI) risk often frame artificial superintelligence as a problem of value alignment: the central task is to ensure that advanced systems act in accordance with human intentions or moral principles. This article argues that such a framing is necessary but insufficient. The danger posed by artificial superintelligence is not merely that it may pursue the wrong values, but that it may introduce a new concentration of autonomous and potentially dominating power. Drawing on political realism in both political theory and international relations, we reinterpret AI catastrophic risk as a structural problem of power under anarchy. The core concerns of AI safety—instrumental convergence, race dynamics, and loss of control—already rely on implicitly realist assumptions about survival, self-help, and the pursuit of power. Yet proposed solutions often retreat into moralism, asking states, firms, or machines to behave ethically without sufficiently altering the incentives that drive competitive acceleration. Against both moralistic reassurance and fatalistic resignation, we argue that realism offers a constructive response. Fear can coordinate divided actors when a threat is perceived as immediate, symmetric, and visible. Artificial superintelligence plausibly satisfies the first two conditions: current evidence of strategic deception and agentic misalignment suggests a shortening temporal horizon, while loss-of-control dynamics would expose even first movers to subordination. What is missing is political visibility. The task of AI governance is therefore to create common knowledge of ASI as a prospective hegemonic threat through shared evaluations, mandatory incident reporting, and institutionalized transparency of peril. The aim is not to moralize machines, but to organize power before it becomes uncontrollable.

title: Employment-access constraints in the 15-minute city
source: Environment and Planning B Urban Analytics and City Science
summary: The “15-minute city” has emerged as an influential urban-planning paradigm, promoting proximity to work and essential services. Its feasibility for journey-to-work commuting, however, has rarely been examined quantitatively. Here, we show t
content: The “15-minute city” has emerged as an influential urban-planning paradigm, promoting proximity to work and essential services. Its feasibility for journey-to-work commuting, however, has rarely been examined quantitatively. Here, we show that employment proximity is constrained by heterogeneity in the number of employees per firm. Combining urban geometry with empirically observed firm-size distributions, we derive a lower bound on commuting time that holds even under optimal workplace placement. This bound reveals a sharp transition: when employment is sufficiently unevenly distributed across firms, no spatial rearrangement of workplaces can provide uniformly short commutes. Applied to Paris and its near suburbs, with area A = 762 km 2 and empirical firm-size exponent γ ^ ≃ 1.38 , the model predicts that only about 37% of workers can reach their workplace within 15 minutes by walking. Cycling increases this share to about 67%, but still leaves roughly one third of the workforce beyond the 15-minute threshold. Achieving universal short commutes would therefore require economic restructuring, differentiated mobility strategies, remote work, or a longer target time. Our results suggest replacing the universal 15-minute target, for commuting, by a city-specific benchmark determined by firm-size heterogeneity and urban scale.

title: Partial Disruptions and Recovery Strategies in Vegetable Supply Chains under Heavy Rainfall: The Role of Irrational Purchasing Decisions
source: Academic journal of management and social sciences
summary: Heavy rainfall may impair a vegetable supply chain without shutting down the market. This paper studies that partial state and the part played by non-routine purchasing during disruption and recovery. The system dynamics model follows veget
content: Heavy rainfall may impair a vegetable supply chain without shutting down the market. This paper studies that partial state and the part played by non-routine purchasing during disruption and recovery. The system dynamics model follows vegetables through farmers, distribution centers, and retailers. Rainfall-related losses in production and transport enter the same structure as deterioration, inventory adjustment, price, and demand. We compare seven scenarios. They cover normal operation, two disruption intensities, and excessive or suppressed purchasing at each intensity. Capacity falls and the supply gap grows as the rainfall shock becomes more severe; operating cost rises and total profit declines. Purchasing behavior does not change realized production capacity in the model. It changes when and how much consumers demand, which then affects prices and the supply-demand balance. Advance purchasing creates a sharp short-run gap. Suppressed purchasing reduces that pressure, although lower sales and narrower margins may reduce profit. The recovery implication depends on the source of the imbalance. Production protection and transport coordination address the physical shock, while inventory rules and consumer communication address the response to it. The model therefore adds a behavioral demand channel to operations-research analysis of climate-related disruption in perishable food systems.

title: UAV and Advanced Air Mobility for Remote and Inter-Island Connectivity: A Systematic Literature Review
source: Aviation Electronics Information Technology Telecommunications Electricals Controls (AVITEC)
summary: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and advanced air mobility (AAM) offer potential alternatives for improving cargo and passenger transport in regions where conventional transport is constrained by distance, terrain, and fragmented geography.
content: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and advanced air mobility (AAM) offer potential alternatives for improving cargo and passenger transport in regions where conventional transport is constrained by distance, terrain, and fragmented geography. This study systematically reviews the use of UAV and AAM systems for connectivity in remote, rural, and inter-island settings. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searches were conducted in Scopus and Google Scholar through Publish or Perish. Of the 3,561 records identified, 74 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2016 and 2026 met the eligibility criteria. The evidence was synthesised narratively and supported by descriptive frequency analysis and bibliometric mapping using VOSviewer. Unlike earlier reviews that primarily examine urban air mobility, last-mile delivery, or medical-drone applications, this review jointly evaluates cargo and passenger transport, supporting infrastructure, and operational challenges from the perspective of remote and archipelagic connectivity. Cargo and goods transport accounts for 92% of the included studies, whereas passenger transport represents only approximately 1%. Multirotor platforms are the most frequently identified aircraft type, while weather, regulatory and airspace constraints, and limited supporting infrastructure are the leading operational challenges. The findings show that passenger-oriented and inter-island applications remain substantially underexplored and require field-based validation, particularly in archipelagic regions.

title: A Quadrilateral Evolutionary Game Analysis of Industrial Wastewater Treatment in China Under the Background of Collaborative Governance
summary: ABSTRACT This study develops a quadrilateral evolutionary game model to examine strategic interactions and system evolution among the central government, local governments, polluting enterprises and the public in industrial wastewater treat
content: ABSTRACT This study develops a quadrilateral evolutionary game model to examine strategic interactions and system evolution among the central government, local governments, polluting enterprises and the public in industrial wastewater treatment (IWWT) under collaborative governance in China. Numerical simulations use official Chinese statistical data related to IWWT, supplemented by parameters from relevant literature. Results show that (1) Increasing central government punishment for incomplete local regulation, expanding special funds and strengthening central supervision can enhance local governments' regulatory enforcement while also incentivising polluting enterprises to implement wastewater treatment. (2) From reducing the environmental tax to increasing special funds share and then increasing the penalty, enterprises' treatment willingness shows an increasing trend. (3) Treatment costs and benefits significantly affect strategic decisions of polluting enterprises. Even with stricter local government regulations, enterprises still adhere loosely when costs are high. (4) Public supervision accelerates convergence towards the optimal‐stable strategy and reduces local governments' regulatory costs.

title: Concentration Strategy and Organizational Performance: A study of Beloxxi industries limited, Ogun State, Nigerian
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
summary: Purpose: This study examines the effect of Concentration Strategy on the organizational performance of Beloxxi Industries Limited in Ogun State, Nigeria. Methodology: A survey was conducted with 161 respondents and data were analyzed using
content: Purpose: This study examines the effect of Concentration Strategy on the organizational performance of Beloxxi Industries Limited in Ogun State, Nigeria. Methodology: A survey was conducted with 161 respondents and data were analyzed using multiple regression. Findings: findings revealed that Product Concentration (p = 0.000), Market Concentration (p = 0.013), Resource Concentration (p = 0.026), and Strategic Alliances (p = 0.000) all had p-values below the 0.05 significance level, indicating that each factor significantly and positively affects organizational performance. Originality/Value: This revealed that, a balanced concentration strategy is essential for enhancing performance, as evidenced by Beloxxi Industries. It was recommends that firms should focus on developing and promoting core products that align with consumer demand to optimize resources and improve market penetration. Additionally, investing in market research to target high-growth segments, adopting lean management practices for efficient resource use, and nurturing strategic alliances to boost competitive advantage are advised. These strategies collectively enhance organizational performance, demonstrating their importance in manufacturing firms like Beloxxi Industries.

title: “Green Bankruptcy”: A Study on the Legal Mechanisms for Priority Satisfaction of Environmental Claims in Corporate Bankruptcy Reorganization
summary: The priority‑of‑repayment right for environmental claims is vital to protecting environmental interests and advancing ecological conservation. Nevertheless, China’s Enterprise Bankruptcy Law contains no specific rules on environmental claim
content: The priority‑of‑repayment right for environmental claims is vital to protecting environmental interests and advancing ecological conservation. Nevertheless, China’s Enterprise Bankruptcy Law contains no specific rules on environmental claims, and the ongoing revision of the Bankruptcy Law has not adequately addressed this issue, which misaligns with the country’s ecological‑civilization drive and green socioeconomic transition. In judicial practice, people’s courts usually classify environmental tort claims as ordinary bankruptcy claims. Ranked low in the repayment hierarchy, such claims frequently see low recovery rates. This fails to redress losses suffered by environmental tort creditors and may enable enterprises to dodge environmental liabilities via bankruptcy. Against this backdrop, it is imperative to explore and build a legal mechanism guaranteeing effective satisfaction of environmental claims in corporate bankruptcy. It will protect environmental creditors’ rights, refine the bankruptcy legal system, and underpin ecological‑civilization construction for a “Beautiful China.”

title: Determinants of Going Concern Opinion: The Moderating Role of Managerial Ownership in Basic Materials Sector Companies
source: Journal of Economic and Business Advancement
summary: This study aims to examine the determinants of going concern opinion by analyzing the effects of operating cash flow, financial distress, and sustainability report disclosure, while investigating the moderating role of managerial ownership.
content: This study aims to examine the determinants of going concern opinion by analyzing the effects of operating cash flow, financial distress, and sustainability report disclosure, while investigating the moderating role of managerial ownership. This research employs a quantitative approach using logistic regression and moderated regression analysis, with data processing conducted through STATA 15. The sample consists of 74 basic materials sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2020–2024 period, resulting in 370 firm-year observations. The findings indicate that operating cash flow and financial distress have significant negative effects on going concern opinion, while sustainability report disclosure has a negative but insignificant effect. Managerial ownership does not moderate the relationship between operating cash flow or financial distress and going concern opinion, but significantly moderates the relationship between sustainability report disclosure and going concern opinion. These findings highlight that auditors continue to emphasize financial indicators in evaluating business continuity, while ownership structure influences the credibility of sustainability-related information. The study provides practical implications for corporate managers in improving financial resilience and strengthening disclosure quality to support stakeholder confidence. This study contributes to agency theory and signaling theory by providing empirical evidence on how financial conditions and governance mechanisms shape going concern assessments in emerging markets.

title: Developing Integrated Project Management Models for Large- Scale Affordable Housing Initiatives
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
summary: The growing global demand for affordable housing has led to a need for innovative and efficient project management strategies, particularly for large-scale initiatives aimed at addressing housing shortages in underserved communities. This p
content: The growing global demand for affordable housing has led to a need for innovative and efficient project management strategies, particularly for large-scale initiatives aimed at addressing housing shortages in underserved communities. This paper examines the complexities of managing large-scale affordable housing projects, focusing on challenges such as cost overruns, delays, inefficient resource allocation, and stakeholder coordination. It explores integrated project management models that combine traditional practices with cutting-edge technologies, such as Building Information Modeling (BIM), AI-driven analytics, and cloud-based tracking systems, to optimize project execution and improve overall outcomes. Through a detailed literature review and framework analysis, the paper identifies essential components of successful project management, including stakeholder engagement, financial planning, supply chain coordination, and quality control. The research highlights the importance of sustainability and compliance within project management frameworks and how emerging technologies can address regulatory complexities and enhance project transparency. It further investigates the barriers to adopting new technologies, such as infrastructure constraints and financial limitations, and proposes practical solutions, including publicprivate partnerships, financial risk-sharing models, and capacity-building strategies for project teams. The paper concludes by providing recommendations for future research in AIdriven project optimization, real-time risk assessment, and the development of smart governance frameworks. These insights contribute to the development of more scalable, sustainable, and efficient housing solutions, offering pathways for addressing the affordable housing crisis globally.

title: Aiding or shaming in climate politics: Evidence from a survey experiment in Brazil
summary: Emerging economies face substantial pressure from some other countries to reform their climate policies and practices. Few countries have faced greater foreign criticism than Brazil. What are the effects of these foreign interventions on Br
content: Emerging economies face substantial pressure from some other countries to reform their climate policies and practices. Few countries have faced greater foreign criticism than Brazil. What are the effects of these foreign interventions on Brazilian citizens’ climate policy opinions? In a preregistered survey experiment, the effects of prompts about foreign aid and international shame from prominent actors on citizens’ attitudes toward various climate policies are examined. The results show Brazilians perceive climate aid as fairer than international shaming, but neither intervention shifts average policy support much, except shaming only marginally reduces support for a carbon tax. Effects emerge, however, when disaggregating by respondents’ prior environmental attitudes: foreign aid increases support for several policies among environmentally conscious citizens while decreasing it among those with weaker environmental attitudes, a polarizing pattern shaming also produces, though more modestly and for fewer policies.
